contract.settlement_definition: Each award, selection or draft market settles Yes only if the named player (or team/pick slot) is the one officially announced for the stated season or draft; the sampled award rules say Yes if the player 'wins' the award in the 2026-27 season, monthly awards are named per conference and month (KXNBADPOTM: 'Western Conference Defensive Player of the Month ... in October/November'), the draft-pick rule says Yes if the named prospect is selected at the stated slot, and the Hall of Fame rule says Yes if the person is 'announced as an inductee' for the 2027 class and No if the class is announced without him. There is no OT/DNP concept; co-winners split the Yes payout $1/N rounded down to the cent where the rule says so (most sampled award rules; not KXNBASIXTH or the Hall of Fame). After the reconciliation the key holds 64 series (14 with sampled rules) generated by six processes: the media-ballot election (s1-s4), the draft and lottery (s5), the All-Star composite (s6), series and tournament MVPs (s7: Finals, conference finals and Cup MVP) and committee, nominee and peer-vote awards including the Hall of Fame (s8).

rules_evidence.quote: wins the Pro Basketball Clutch Player of the Year in the 2026-27 season, then the market resolves to Yes
rules_evidence.establishes: Award markets are single-winner-by-name with the season stated explicitly; the sampled text restates no minimum-games or eligibility condition, so whether league eligibility rules govern this award is not stated (an inference, not established by the quote).

rules_evidence.quote: positions will pay $1/N (rounded down to the nearest cent), where N is the number of awarded players
rules_evidence.establishes: Ties/co-winners split the Yes payout equally and round down, so a tie lowers the realised value of a Yes below $1 and makes P(win) different from expected payout.

rules_evidence.quote: is selected as the 1st overall pick in the 2027 Pro Basketball Draft, then the market resolves to Yes
rules_evidence.establishes: Draft markets settle on the player selected at the stated slot; the sampled text is silent on a traded pick, a prospect withdrawing and a rescheduled draft, so settlement on the player actually chosen is an inference (u7).

rules_evidence.quote: wins the Western Conference Defensive Player of the Month award in October/November
rules_evidence.establishes: Monthly awards are separate per-conference markets with a named window (October/November combined), so there is no cross-conference tie and the exposure window is the games in that span.

rules_evidence.quote: If the inductees are announced by any of the Source Agencies and Terry Stotts is not included, the market will resolve to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: Hall of Fame markets settle on inclusion in a class of several inductees (no $1/N split), so candidates do not exclude each other and the target is a committee election for each person.

rules_evidence.quote: wins the Pro Basketball Finals MVP in the 2026-27 season
rules_evidence.establishes: Finals MVP is a single-winner award decided after the Finals, so its probability is the product of the team winning the series and the player being chosen from that roster.

variants_and_edge_cases: Co-winner or tie: most sampled award rules (KXNBACLUTCH, KXNBACUPMVP, KXNBAEXEC, KXNBAFINMVP, KXNBAMIMP, KXNBASJC, conference-finals MVPs) pay $1/N rounded down; monthly awards are per-conference markets (KXNBADPOTM, KXNBAROTM) with the same $1/N clause for multiple recipients, KXNBASIXTH's sampled text has no tie clause, and Hall of Fame classes have several inductees who each settle Yes independently.

Eligibility gates (65-game and 20-minute rule) are enforced by the league and, if they govern the market, can disqualify an MVP-calibre candidate after the market has priced him; the sampled text does not say which awards they govern or whether Kalshi follows the league on eligibility.
Draft-slot markets (KXNBADRAFT1..10, KXNBADRAFTPICK) settle on who is picked at slot N whichever team holds it; team-to-draft and lottery markets settle on pick ownership or lottery result instead.

Group markets (All-NBA teams, All-Star starters, award finalists, lottery picks) are nested or cumulative sets of the same latent ranking, so rung probabilities must be monotone and sum to the set size.

Only 14 of the 64 live series have sampled rules; the 50 others (All-NBA teams, All-Star, draft comparison/category/international/conference, lottery odds and others) are TITLE_ONLY and their tie and cutoff wording is not visible.
contract.settlement_data_source: League official announcements: voting-result releases for awards and All-NBA, All-Star starters announcement, draft lottery broadcast and the draft transaction record.

mechanism.summary: These contracts resolve through human processes whose inputs arrive at different clocks. Awards are a ranked-ballot election: a panel of media voters ranks five candidates (points 10-7-5-3-1) after the season, so the winner is the candidate with the greatest points, which depends on (a) who is eligible after the games/minutes minimum, (b) the candidates' perceived production relative to the field, (c) team success which voters treat as a prerequisite, and (d) vote splitting among near-equal candidates and voter fatigue for repeat winners. Selection markets (All-NBA, All-Star, All-Defensive, All-Rookie) are nested cut lines on the same points ranking. Monthly awards depend on the games actually played in a calendar window. Draft markets are a different chain: lottery draw and pick ownership (protections, swaps) decide which team holds slot N, then team preference, workouts and trade activity decide who is selected. Outcomes are lumpy (one winner), early prices drift on narrative, and the most informative single observable is eligibility, which can flip an outcome from near-certain to impossible. All-Star selection is a separate process: a 50% fan, 25% player and 25% media weighted-rank composite fills starter slots by position group and conference, and conference coaches then pick reserves (stage s6). Series MVPs (Finals, conference finals, Cup) are a third process: a small media panel picks a player almost always from the winning side right after the deciding game, so P(MVP) = P(team wins) x P(chosen | team wins). Committee and peer-vote honours (Hall of Fame, Social Justice Champion, Teammate and Sportsmanship awards) are nominee elections with their own panels and calendars.

stages.name: Eligibility and games-played gate
stages.description: A candidate must clear league thresholds (65 games with at least 20 minutes in the current CBA for major awards and All-NBA, role rules such as bench-starts for Sixth Man, rookie status for ROY, clutch minimum for Clutch POY, qualifying-games rule for stat leaders). The state is a running ledger that moves with each injury, rest night and minute total, and the cost of a missed qualifying game is permanent. Probability of crossing the line depends on games remaining and injury hazard, not on the season-to-date average. The 65-game rule is described from memory of the league criteria; which awards it governs is not established here: the monthly awards, Coach and Executive of the Year, the All-Star selection and the draft are not governed by it, and the 15-19 minute allowance and the Clutch and All-Rookie specifics are unverified (u3).
stages.distribution: Bimodal near the line: mass near 0 or 1 for most players, with a narrow band of players with zero slack whose probability is a binomial-style survival over remaining games and injury hazard.

stages.name: Perceived production versus the field
stages.description: Voters rank on points, rebounds, assists, efficiency summaries and advanced numbers, but also on role-specific awards: defensive reputation and block/steal counts for DPOY, improvement delta versus the previous season for MIP, rookie rank for ROY. The relevant quantity is the gap to the next-best candidate on the stats voters actually look at, not the candidate's absolute level, and the stats used by voters are not identical to RAPM-type impact models.
stages.distribution: Heavy right tail in the leader's margin; the winner's vote share is typically concentrated (first-place votes dominated by one or two names) so P(win) behaves like a softmax over a small candidate set.

stages.name: Team success and narrative conditioning
stages.description: Historical winners overwhelmingly come from top seeds, and the penalty for a lower seed is steep for MVP/DPOY while smaller for ROY; coach and executive awards are driven by wins relative to preseason expectation, not wins alone. Late-season stories (a surge, a record chase, a voter-fatigue narrative about a repeat winner) can reverse a small metric gap, and voters' ballots are submitted before the playoffs.
stages.distribution: Step-like in team seed and approximately logistic in the gap between win total and preseason expectation; narrative shocks are rare and large.

stages.name: Ballot aggregation and cut lines
stages.description: Final standings are the sum of points across about 100 ballots, with ties broken by rule or shared payout; All-NBA and similar teams are cut lines on the same ranking (positionless since 2023-24), so P(1st team) is nested inside P(any team). Vote splitting between two similar candidates (two centers, two rookies) reduces both below what each would earn alone.
stages.distribution: Discrete, bounded sum of ranks; winner and cut-line events are strongly negatively correlated across candidates; nested sets must satisfy monotone sums.

stages.name: Draft order and selection
stages.description: Lottery order is a draw from published odds that depend on final standings (and tie-break coin flips); pick ownership then passes through protections, swaps and conveyance rules that may take years to resolve. Given owner and slot, selection depends on consensus board rank and its dispersion, team need, workout and medical information, and the probability that the pick is traded and the trade partner picks a different player. Settlement is on the player actually named.
stages.distribution: Lottery is a known discrete probability table; selection among the top few prospects is a categorical mixture whose entropy falls sharply in the final 48 hours.

stages.name: All-Star selection: weighted vote composite, positional slots and coach reserves
stages.description: All-Star starters are fixed by a composite of three electorates, not a media ballot: fan vote 50%, current players 25% and media 25%, combined as weighted ranks within guard and frontcourt groups per conference (two backcourt and three frontcourt starters). The fan share is public in early-return snapshots, moves with market size and social following, and can place a less productive player in a slot; reserves are then chosen by conference coaches (seven per conference, two of them wildcards) who weight production and team record, and injured selectees are replaced by the commissioner. KXNBAASSTARTERS, KXNBAALLSTARS and KXNBAALLSTAR therefore need fan-return dynamics, the weighted-rank arithmetic and a separate coach-vote model.
stages.distribution: Weighted-rank composite with a random-walk fan component that shrinks as the voting window closes; discrete slot allocation (5 starters and 7 reserves per conference) with correlated displacement within a position group.

stages.name: Series and tournament MVP conditional on the winning side
stages.description: Finals MVP, the two conference-finals MVPs (awarded since 2022) and the Cup MVP are voted by a small media panel immediately after the deciding game, and the winner almost always comes from the team that won (the only losing-team Finals MVP was in 1969). The probability therefore factors into the chance the team wins the series or the Cup knockout (bracket path, home court, series length, neutral-site single games for the Cup) and the chance the panel picks this player given a win, which follows his share of the winning team's series scoring and pre-series best-player status; a dominant star takes most of the conditional mass, a balanced roster splits it. Prices move game by game as both factors update.
stages.distribution: Product of a series-win Bernoulli and a categorical over two to four candidates on the winning roster, highly concentrated on the top scorer; small co-MVP mass for the $1/N clause.

stages.name: Committee, nominee and peer-vote honours including the Hall of Fame
stages.description: The Hall of Fame (KXNBAHALLOFFAME) inducts a class through a screening committee that names finalists, usually at All-Star weekend, and an honors committee whose supermajority vote is announced in early April, with direct-elect committees for veterans, contributors and international candidates bypassing the finalist stage; coaches such as the sampled candidate follow the coach path. The Social Justice Champion is chosen by a league committee from team nominees and finalists, and the Teammate and Sportsmanship awards by player votes among finalists. These outcomes depend on nominee status, career markers and committee composition, not on game production in the market window, and the finalist announcement is the main information jump.
stages.distribution: Two-stage Bernoulli (finalist, then elected) for the Hall of Fame with no fixed class size; categorical over five or so finalists for the nominee awards, with a small co-winner probability.

talent_strength.note: Candidate production and impact; impact metrics are secondary because voters use box-score and reputation.

opponent_matchup.note: Awards and draft slots are season-long or one-off events decided by a ballot or a lottery, so no head-to-head opponent exists; the nearest analogue is field competition, handled in s4 under nba.allnba_points_ladder.

role_personnel.note: Role definitions (bench, rookie, clutch minutes) and prospect fit decide who is in the candidate set.

availability_news.note: Eligibility ledger and injury hazard determine whether the candidate remains in the field.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach of the Year is voted on win totals versus expectation rather than on a measurable scheme variable; scheme effects enter through wins in nba.expectation_overperformance, so no separate scheme input is warranted for award or draft ballots.

environment.note: Venue, altitude and weather play no part in a vote or a lottery draw; the only environmental channel is schedule strength feeding wins, covered by nba.standings_sim.

game_context_script.note: Late-season trajectory and storyline before ballots are cast.

pace_volume.note: Volume matters only through counting-stat totals inside nba.award_stats; there is no per-event opportunity count that a pace input would scale in these markets.

efficiency_conversion.note: Shooting efficiency and defensive metrics are summary inputs voters read.

distribution_variance.note: Ballot-sum distribution and board dispersion define tails and cut-line probabilities.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Seeding and games-in-window for monthly awards.

officiating_rules.note: League eligibility rules act as the rule layer for awards.

settlement_contract.note: Co-winner pro-rata and slot-based settlement; remaining series are TITLE_ONLY.

nba.eligibility_minutes_ledger.label: Qualifying-games ledger (65 games with 20+ minutes) and slack
nba.eligibility_minutes_ledger.mechanism: The award eligibility count is a deterministic ledger that only the league's definition of a qualifying game updates; slack to the line plus injury hazard gives the probability of staying eligible.
nba.eligibility_minutes_ledger.rationale: The existing eligibility input restates the rule but not the arithmetic; a player at 50 qualifying games with 20 left has a very different conditional risk from one at 62 with a nagging injury, and games of 15-20 minutes count only in a small allowance.
nba.eligibility_minutes_ledger.measurement: Per player: qualifying = games with minutes >= 20 (allow up to 2 games of 15-20 minutes per league rule, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for the 2026-27 rule); slack = games_remaining - (65 - qualifying); P(eligible) = P(missed games among remaining <= slack) under a Poisson-binomial with per-game miss probability = player-season availability rate shrunk with k=20 games toward position prior, updated nightly after the 6pm ET injury report; as-of timestamp = last completed game. Apply the ledger only to awards the league criteria say it governs (flag per award; SOURCE_UNVERIFIED), and not to monthly awards, Coach or Executive of the Year, All-Star selection or draft markets.
nba.eligibility_minutes_ledger.why: MVP, All-NBA, DPOY and Clutch markets can flip from near-certain to impossible on one game, so the ledger is the first gate for every candidate price.

nba.award_role_filters.label: Award-specific candidate filters (bench-start ratio, rookie status, clutch minimum)
nba.award_role_filters.mechanism: Each award has a definitional filter (Sixth Man must come off the bench in more games than he starts, ROY needs rookie status, Clutch POY needs clutch minutes/games, MIP needs improvement versus prior year) that decides who is in the candidate set.
nba.award_role_filters.rationale: A single input called award_stats treats all awards alike, but the candidate set is built by the filter first; a starter promoted mid-season loses Sixth Man eligibility, and a rookie who played overseas may or may not be a rookie.
nba.award_role_filters.measurement: Per award: boolean membership computed from the league definition on as-of date: sixth man requires games_off_bench > games_started; ROY requires rookie flag from the league rookie list; Clutch POY requires clutch minutes (last 5 min, score within 5) >= league minimum; produce candidate list and the gap in the stat the award names (clutch net points, improvement delta in PER/BPM, defensive win shares) with 10-game shrinkage to season value.
nba.award_role_filters.why: The candidate field and the named statistic differ per series, so a single production metric misranks Sixth Man, Clutch and MIP contenders.

nba.expectation_overperformance.label: Wins minus preseason expectation (own, non-market)
nba.expectation_overperformance.mechanism: Coach, Executive, MIP and team-driven awards reward results above what the roster implied before the season, so voters compare wins to a preseason baseline.
nba.expectation_overperformance.rationale: Total wins alone ranks the best teams first, but Coach of the Year goes to the largest positive surprise; the baseline must be an own rating-based preseason projection and not a sportsbook win total to avoid a market-derived input.
nba.expectation_overperformance.measurement: exp_wins_pre = 82 x (own preseason team rating converted via Pythagorean with exponent 14, using returning minutes-weighted player ratings with 0.6 weight on last season, 0.4 on career, regressed 30% to league mean); surprise = wins_to_date - exp_wins_pre scaled by sd 6 wins; recompute on the as-of date using games played to date + 82 - GP times current rating.
nba.expectation_overperformance.why: Coach of the Year, Executive of the Year and MIP prices should key off surprise rather than wins; the existing catalog has no baseline for it.

nba.allnba_points_ladder.label: All-NBA points ladder and cut-line margins (positionless)
nba.allnba_points_ladder.mechanism: All-NBA teams are three five-player cut lines on a single points ranking (5/3/1 for first/second/third team); a candidate's probabilities across team markets are nested.
nba.allnba_points_ladder.rationale: Candidates with similar profiles split votes and a margin of a few points moves a player between teams; ballots are positionless since 2023-24, so the old guard/forward/center constraints no longer bind and should not be modelled.
nba.allnba_points_ladder.measurement: Simulate 100 ballots: each voter draws a ranked 15-player list from a Dirichlet-perturbed consensus of candidates' production and team-success scores (concentration alpha=8 per candidate, calibrated to 2023-25 published vote totals); output P(rank<=5), P(rank<=10), P(rank<=15), enforce sums of 5, 10, 15; as-of nightly after the eligibility filter.
free_sources: Official All-NBA voting totals (published after announcement)
nba.allnba_points_ladder.why: Rung markets on 1st/2nd/3rd team are cumulative on the same ranking and need an enforced consistent ladder, which the market's independent quotes may violate.

nba.draft_pick_ownership_graph.label: Draft pick ownership graph with protections and swaps
nba.draft_pick_ownership_graph.mechanism: Which franchise holds slot N depends on lottery results filtered through traded-pick protections, swap rights and conveyance order across years.
nba.draft_pick_ownership_graph.rationale: Team-to-draft and slot markets require knowing owner(s) and conditions; an unconditional top-4 protected pick converts to a future obligation and changes incentives of both teams in the standings race.
nba.draft_pick_ownership_graph.measurement: Table per pick: original team, current owner, protection (top-N range), swap counterpart and conveyance date; for each lottery outcome, determine slot and holder using the protection rules; as-of timestamp = latest completed trade; join with simulated standings to yield P(owner holds slot k).
nba.draft_pick_ownership_graph.why: Pick-slot and team-to-draft markets settle on ownership as much as on prospect choice, and traded protections create incentives that move standings.

nba.prospect_board_dispersion.label: Prospect consensus rank and cross-board dispersion
nba.prospect_board_dispersion.mechanism: Selection at slot N is a categorical outcome over the top prospects; disagreement across public boards and team-specific mocks signals entropy and information arrival.
nba.prospect_board_dispersion.rationale: A single consensus rank hides that the second pick is nearly deterministic in some drafts and a coin flip among four prospects in others; measuring dispersion is the correct uncertainty input.
nba.prospect_board_dispersion.measurement: For each prospect: mean and sd of rank across at least 6 boards (ESPN, The Athletic, Tankathon, NBADraft.net, Bleacher Report, Yahoo) with weights proportional to each source's historical rank-error; convert to P(selected at slot k) by a Plackett-Luce model fit on 2015-2025 drafts; update after each workout/medical report with 48h half-life.
nba.prospect_board_dispersion.why: Draft slot markets on picks 1-10 are priced as separate coins; the Plackett-Luce structure enforces that one prospect fills one slot.

nba.monthly_window_schedule.label: Games-in-window and schedule for monthly awards
nba.monthly_window_schedule.mechanism: Monthly player/rookie/coach/defender awards depend on games played inside the window, with fewer games for a candidate lowering his total counting stats and chance of an extreme month.
nba.monthly_window_schedule.rationale: Players on teams with 12 games in the window versus 16 have different expected volume; the conference split of winners and ties matters for pro-rata payout.
nba.monthly_window_schedule.measurement: games_in_window per candidate team from the league schedule; expected counting stats = per-game mean x games with 10-game shrinkage; probability of winning within conference = softmax over candidates of standardized (points, wins, efficiency) with temperature fit on past months; update on the as-of date.
nba.monthly_window_schedule.why: Monthly series are decided in a fixed short window where a schedule difference of three games matters.

nba.allstar_fan_vote_composite.label: All-Star starter composite (fan 50% / player 25% / media 25%) and positional slot arithmetic
nba.allstar_fan_vote_composite.mechanism: Starters are the top weighted-average ranks within position groups per conference: each candidate's rank in the fan vote, the current-player vote and the media vote is combined 50/25/25 and the best composite fill two backcourt and three frontcourt slots in each conference.
nba.allstar_fan_vote_composite.rationale: KXNBAASSTARTERS, KXNBAALLSTARS and KXNBAALLSTAR are not decided by the ballot of about 100 media voters in stage s4: the fan vote carries half the weight, is public in early-return snapshots during the voting window, and depends on market size and social following, while the player and media votes follow production. The slot arithmetic (guard versus frontcourt, per conference) decides who is displaced.
nba.allstar_fan_vote_composite.measurement: For each candidate and conference compute composite = 0.50 x fan_rank + 0.25 x player_rank + 0.25 x media_rank within the guard or frontcourt group; fan_rank at close = last published early-return rank plus a random-walk adjustment scaled by the share of voting window remaining (estimate step variance from past years' return snapshots), with the prior from last year's final fan rank, market size and social following; player and media ranks from the production rank in nba.award_stats with beta noise estimated from past ballot-vs-stat rank gaps; starters = lowest composites filling 2 guard and 3 frontcourt slots per conference (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for the 2027 formula and slot split); simulate 10,000 draws and report P(starter) per candidate.
free_sources: Wayback Machine snapshots of fan-vote leaderboards
raw_data: fan vote early-return snapshots by date
final fan, player and media ranks by candidate
nba.allstar_fan_vote_composite.why: Carries the dominant 50% fan component and slot arithmetic that the media-ballot stage omits, which is the mechanism behind the live starters and All-Stars series.

nba.allstar_reserve_coach_vote.label: All-Star reserve selection by coaches (7 per conference) and injury replacement
nba.allstar_reserve_coach_vote.mechanism: After starters are fixed, conference head coaches vote for seven reserves each (not their own players) and the commissioner names injury replacements, so P(All-Star) for a non-starter is the chance of ranking among the best remaining players by position and wildcard slots.
nba.allstar_reserve_coach_vote.rationale: KXNBAALLSTARS and KXNBAALLSTAR settle on the full roster, so reserve probability matters as much as starter probability; coaches value team record and recent play more than fan appeal, and an injured selectee is replaced by a commissioner choice that is hard to forecast.
nba.allstar_reserve_coach_vote.measurement: For each non-starter candidate: coach-vote score = z-score of production rank (nba.award_stats) plus team win% rank, calibrated to past reserve selections by logistic regression on 10 seasons with position group and conference as strata; P(reserve) = P(rank among the 7 reserve slots after starters are removed) via 10,000 simulations conditional on the starter simulation; injury-replacement probability = P(a selectee is injured) x P(commissioner picks the next-ranked player); the 2 wildcard slots are position-free (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for 2027 rules).
nba.allstar_reserve_coach_vote.why: Reserves are decided by a different electorate than starters and by a different rule, and the roster markets need both.

nba.voter_signal_proxy.label: Observable voter-signal proxy: public media ladders, prior-win count and repeat-winner penalty
nba.voter_signal_proxy.mechanism: Replaces the unmeasurable narrative and voter-fatigue notion with observables: average rank in published media award ladders and straw polls, the number of consecutive prior wins, and the candidate's first-place share in the previous two seasons.
nba.voter_signal_proxy.rationale: nba.voting_narrative is audited WEAK because it is not measurable as defined, yet narrative and fatigue are the only drivers of the vote beyond production and team success; a proxy built from public ladders and past ballots gives them a measurable form without using any market price.
nba.voter_signal_proxy.measurement: For each candidate and award: mean rank over the last 4 published media ladders (NBA.com ladder, ESPN straw poll; unranked = 6th) with weights 0.4/0.3/0.2/0.1 newest first; repeat_penalty = number of consecutive prior wins; prior_share = first-place vote share in the last two seasons (0 if not a finalist); fit a conditional-logit ballot model on 2000-2026 winners with these three features plus production rank and seed, shrinking coefficients with a ridge penalty chosen by leave-one-season-out.
nba.voter_signal_proxy.why: Gives the narrative and voter-fatigue effects an observable form for MVP, DPOY, ROY and similar awards.

nba.all_star_process.label: All-Star voting/selection, captains and event participation
nba.all_star_process.mechanism: Fan/player/media voting and league announcements determine starters, reserves, contest entrants and event outcomes.
nba.all_star_process.rationale: All-Star outcomes are driven by published vote tallies (fan, player, media weights), selection rules and injuries/availability; event participation announcements are dated and sourced. Subtle: weights and eligibility rules change by year and the market often resolves on official announcement wording.
nba.all_star_process.measurement: Public vote leaderboards over time, weight formula, historical rank-to-selection conversion, injury status and eligibility; for contests, announced participants and past winners' profiles.
nba.all_star_process.why: Captures the All-Star voting calendar, captains and event participation that fix when fan-vote returns and roster announcements arrive; context for the starter and reserve inputs.

nba.title_path.label: Playoff bracket path, matchup and home-court structure
nba.title_path.mechanism: Series winner and title probabilities depend on the bracket path (seed, opponent strength, home-court) and matchup-specific adjustments.
nba.title_path.rationale: Title odds are the product of series-win probabilities along a path that depends on which seed you are, who you face and the rest/injury states. A given team's path difficulty can differ substantially even for equal rating. Subtle: series outcomes are correlated through injuries to key players across rounds.
nba.title_path.measurement: Simulate bracket with seed distribution and series-level win probability; incorporate matchup tweaks (style, pace, rim protection) and home-court structure (2-2-1-1-1).
nba.title_path.why: Series and Cup MVP markets need P(team wins the series or title) as the first factor.

nba.series_model.label: Best-of-seven series model (home-court, game-to-game correlation, adjustments)
nba.series_model.mechanism: Series win and game-count probabilities derive from per-game win probabilities with home pattern; correlated injuries and adjustments change the distribution.
nba.series_model.rationale: A simple independent binomial overstates sweeps vs actual; playoff rotations shorten, pace slows, and stars play more minutes, shifting the effective team rating. Series props (sweep, exact games, player series totals) need game-level scoring simulations. Subtle: in-series injuries and coaching adjustments create positive correlation between games.
nba.series_model.measurement: Per-game win p from playoff-adjusted ratings with home advantage; sample game-to-game correlation parameter; adapt rating after injuries; compute pmf of series length and winner.
nba.series_model.why: Series length and winner per round feed the series-MVP first factor and the number of games a candidate accumulates.
raw_data: playoff game results with home/away and injuries

nba.cup_format.label: NBA Cup group/knockout structure and tiebreakers
nba.cup_format.mechanism: Cup outcomes depend on group-stage point-differential tiebreakers, wildcard rules and single-elimination knockout games, with unusual incentives and neutral sites.
nba.cup_format.rationale: Group-stage point differential makes blowout margins matter in Cup games; rest decisions and star availability vary relative to regular-season games; the knockout games are neutral-site single games. Subtle: rules details change by season and the settlement rule for Cup counts must be read from official documentation.
nba.cup_format.measurement: Enumerate remaining group games with margin/tiebreaker simulation, apply wildcard rules, knockout bracket at neutral site; adjust for star minutes and motivation.
nba.cup_format.why: Cup MVP depends on which team survives the group tiebreaks and neutral-site knockout games.
raw_data: NBA Cup group and knockout results

nba.finals_mvp_given_title_share.label: Probability a given player wins Finals/Conference Finals MVP conditional on his team winning the series
nba.finals_mvp_given_title_share.mechanism: Award contracts are conditional on the team winning and then on voter choice among its players, which follows stat shares and narrative in the series.
nba.finals_mvp_given_title_share.rationale: Finals MVP of a champion usually goes to the top scorer or best player of the series, with media voters weighing series scoring, efficiency and team role; P(player MVP) = P(team wins) x P(player chosen | team wins) and the second factor can be estimated from past award results.
nba.finals_mvp_given_title_share.measurement: From 20 seasons of Finals and Conference Finals results compute for each champion's top-3 players the share of MVP awards by rank in series points, by pre-series team star ranking and by minutes share; fit a conditional logit on pre-series expected points rank and best-player indicator (pre-series BPM rank), regularised; output P(MVP | team wins) by player. Combine with series win probability from the series model. As-of: before series start (updated per game).
nba.finals_mvp_given_title_share.why: Second factor of every series MVP market: P(player chosen | his team wins), driven by series scoring share and best-player status.
raw_data: Finals and conference-finals MVP winners with series box scores

nba.award_vote_and_cowinner_model.label: Voting-panel and nominee model for award contracts, including the probability of multiple co-winners
nba.award_vote_and_cowinner_model.mechanism: Award contracts such as the Social Justice Champion, Finals MVP, conference finals MVP and Cup All-Tournament selections are decided by a panel or vote among nominees, not by team simulation, so the relevant quantities are the nominee set, the historical winner profile and the chance of several winners.
nba.award_vote_and_cowinner_model.rationale: For KXNBASJC the sampled rules split the payout $1/N among multiple awardees, so P(multiple winners) and the winner's profile (community work and nominee status) matter more than basketball production. For Finals and conference finals MVPs the winner is chosen from the winning team after the series by a panel, so the team simulation only gives the first factor. Panels are small, so narrative and series stats can dominate and the winner is a discrete choice among a few candidates.
nba.award_vote_and_cowinner_model.measurement: Build an award history table (at least 15 seasons) of nominees or finalists, winner(s) and the number of awardees. Fit a conditional logit for P(winner | nominee) on prior finalist or winner status, team success, and for series MVPs on series points rank and best-player indicator, with ridge regularisation and a prior weight of 10 award-years. Estimate P(more than one awardee) as the historical frequency with a beta(1,10) prior, and the expected payout as P(win) x E[1/N | win] rounded down to the cent. For game-based MVPs multiply by P(team wins the series) from nba.series_model. As-of: before announcement, updated when finalists are published.
free_sources: NBA.com award announcements and press releases
nba.award_vote_and_cowinner_model.why: Nominee/panel awards (Social Justice Champion, Teammate, Sportsmanship, series MVPs) and the $1/N co-winner payout need a nominee-set and co-winner model.
raw_data: award winners and number of awardees by year

nba.draft_lottery_odds_table.label: Draft lottery combinatorial odds by pre-lottery rank, including ties and the four-pick rule
nba.draft_lottery_odds_table.mechanism: Pick position for non-playoff teams is a random draw with fixed odds by rank (worst three teams each 14.0% for the top pick, no team falling more than four slots, under the current lottery rules (to be re-confirmed for the draft year)), so draft-position contracts reduce to rank odds times a rank distribution.
nba.draft_lottery_odds_table.rationale: Draft top-3/top-5/top-10 contracts are decided by the lottery, which is a known combinatorial mechanism; the uncertainty is the pre-lottery rank (final record, ties, coin flips) and the team's pick ownership, not the draw itself.
nba.draft_lottery_odds_table.measurement: Encode the current lottery's 1,000 (or 14 x ...) combination allocation by rank 1-14, compute exact P(pick k | rank r) for k=1..14 (including the rule that teams cannot fall more than 4 positions and ties in record are broken by random drawing before the lottery); combine with the simulated distribution of final regular-season ranks from the standings simulation (include play-in losers) to get P(top-3 pick | team). As-of: nightly; rules versioned by draft year.
nba.draft_lottery_odds_table.why: KXNBALOTTERYODDS, KXNBATOPPICK and KXNBATOP3 settle on the lottery draw, which is the published odds table applied to the final pre-lottery ranks.
raw_data: published lottery combination table by draft year
final regular-season standings with tiebreak draws

nba.hof_committee_vote_model.label: Hall of Fame election model: finalist stage, honors-committee vote and direct-elect paths
nba.hof_committee_vote_model.mechanism: A candidate is inducted only after reaching the finalist list and then clearing the honors committee's supermajority, or through a direct-elect committee, so P(inductee) = P(finalist) x P(elected | finalist) or the direct-elect probability.
nba.hof_committee_vote_model.rationale: KXNBAHALLOFFAME settles on being announced as an inductee of the 2027 class and resolves No if the class is announced without the person, so the target is a committee election and not an on-court quantity. Class size is not fixed, so candidates do not strictly crowd each other out; the finalist announcement is the largest information jump; coaches, contributors and international players follow different committees and bars, and a candidate's years on the ballot shift the odds.
nba.hof_committee_vote_model.measurement: From the Hall's published finalist lists and inductee classes for at least 15 years, fit two logistic models by category (NBA player, coach, contributor, international, women): P(finalist | eligible) and P(inducted | finalist), on career markers (players: All-NBA selections, titles, All-Star count, career Win Shares; coaches: regular-season wins, playoff series won, titles, seasons as head coach) and years since eligibility, ridge-penalised with a prior weight of 5 classes; direct-elect committee picks are a separate category frequency. As-of: the market timestamp; switch to P(inducted | finalist) once finalists are announced. The vote threshold (recalled as 18 of 24) is unverified (u8).
free_sources: Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame finalist and class announcements (hoophall.com)
raw_data: Hall of Fame finalist lists and inductee classes by year and category
career award, statistic and coaching-record summaries
nba.hof_committee_vote_model.why: KXNBAHALLOFFAME needs P(inductee) through a two-stage committee election that no ballot, draft or All-Star input describes.

nba.award_stats.reason: Production is the base of every ballot but the entry mixes box-score output with narrative and is not award-specific; split by award via nba.award_role_filters.

nba.games_played_eligibility.reason: Hard gate that creates bimodal outcomes; as written it names the 65-game rule but not the 20-minute qualifying definition or slack arithmetic, now supplied by nba.eligibility_minutes_ledger.

nba.voting_narrative.reason: Not measurable as defined; voter composition and narrative need an observable proxy such as past ballot behaviour and repeat-winner history, otherwise it is a placeholder.

nba.standings_sim.reason: Seed matters through a step in historical MVP/DPOY winners and sets lottery odds for draft markets; relevant but works only after conversion to P(top seed) and lottery odds.

nba.player_impact.reason: RAPM/EPM-style impact describes true value but voters read box-score and reputation, so use it to explain mispricing rather than as the main predictor of vote share.

nba.injury_risk_season.reason: Drives the probability of finishing under the games threshold; useful only combined with the exact qualifying slack.

nba.draft_board.reason: Lottery odds and consensus order are the core draft input; relevant only for the draft/lottery series and ignored for awards, and dispersion across boards is missing.

nba.news.reason: Undefined 'transactions, trades, coaching news'; for the draft the actionable subset is trade/pick-conveyance and workout/medical reports, which now have their own inputs.

nba.minutes.reason: Per-game projected minutes (blowout, foul trouble) belong to single-game props; season awards use season totals and the 20-minute qualifying rule only.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price path for award and draft ballots; useful to see when information was absorbed and for calibration labels, but it is an observation of the market, never an explanatory driver of the outcome.

m.rules_text.reason: Versioned rules text defines the settled quantity for award and draft ballots; wording changes between series are the only way to know the target variable, so it is a required contract input, not a feature.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook price for award and draft ballots is a market-derived quantity; keep as a comparison benchmark to measure disagreement, do not use as an input to the probability model.

m.strike_hit_rates.reason: Award and draft markets have one resolution a year per series, so realised frequency by rung is a handful of observations and cannot calibrate anything.

interactions.mechanism: Voters treat team success as a gate: production wins only when the team is a top-two seed, and below that seed the same production sees a sharp discount, especially for MVP and DPOY; the effect is much smaller for ROY and MIP.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit vote share on production gap with a seed-bucket dummy and compare slopes by award across 2000-2025 results; test seed-bucket x gap coefficient.

interactions.mechanism: At zero slack a single missed game removes a candidate completely, so the probability is a step in games remaining rather than a smooth penalty; players with high slack are insulated.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised winner rate across slack buckets 0, 1-3, 4-8, 9+ on historical candidates; look for a discontinuity at slack 0.

interactions.mechanism: Similar candidates split ballot ranks: two centres with equal metrics both fall relative to a lone candidate with the same metrics, and a surplus of strong forwards lowers P(third team) for a marginal one.
interactions.how_to_test: Add the count of candidates with a similar profile within 1 sd as a feature, or simulate ballots to see whether pairwise vote-share correlation is negative. Treat this as a modelling choice (a ballot-split simulation) and validate it on past points distributions rather than assuming the dependence.

interactions.mechanism: Coach of the Year rewards positive surprise but saturates once a team is already a top seed, because a title favourite cannot overperform much; a mid-seed team with a large surprise beats a top seed with a small one.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress COY winner on surprise and seed with a saturating term; compare predictions of winners for teams above 60 wins.

interactions.mechanism: Slot probabilities for prospects depend on who holds the pick: a team with a veteran roster, a rebuilding team and a team trading the pick pick differently, so P(prospect at slot k) is conditional on the holder.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit selection model with owner-type features on past drafts; measure rank-error of consensus by pick holder.

interactions.mechanism: A series MVP needs both his team to win and the panel to pick him, so a star on a modest favourite can be worth less than the second option on a heavy favourite; the product, not either factor, ranks candidates, and both update after every game.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare log loss of P(win) x P(chosen | win) against a model using only individual series production on past Finals and conference-finals MVPs.

nonlinearities.shape: Step function at the threshold (65 qualifying games)
nonlinearities.why: The rule is a hard threshold, so effect on P(win) is zero until the player is within a few games of the line and then collapses; linear injury-risk adjustment would misprice players near the line.

nonlinearities.shape: Step in seed (top-2 vs rest), saturating above
nonlinearities.why: Winners cluster in top seeds, so probability changes little between seed 1 and 2 but falls sharply beyond seed 4; response is closer to a gate than a slope.

nonlinearities.shape: Softmax in the gap to the next candidate
nonlinearities.why: Vote share is concentrated; a candidate's win probability depends on the margin over the runner-up on voter-visible stats rather than the absolute level.

nonlinearities.shape: Entropy collapse near draft night
nonlinearities.why: Selection probability concentrates quickly as boards converge and insiders report, so the dispersion measure should be time-weighted rather than static.

contract.settlement_definition: The sampled live series (KXNBAPRAPROT, a protected points+rebounds+assists contract) settles Yes if the named player records at least the 'N+' combined total (strike 24.5 means 25+) in the single named game. The protected clause converts the contract to the fair price prior to the opening tip when the player enters during the first half but never again after halftime (including overtime) and has not already reached the required total; a player who enters only after halftime settles on actual stats. The sampled text is silent on whether overtime stats count in the total, so inclusion is inferred from official box-score practice, not verified. Postponement within 48 hours stays open; otherwise it resolves to fair price. The unprotected KXNBAPRA text (now sampled) voids at fair price only an inactive or never-on-court player and settles on recorded stats once he enters; KXNBAPR and KXNBAPA remain TITLE_ONLY.

rules_evidence.quote: records 25+ combined points, rebounds, and assists in the San Antonio vs Sacramento Pro Basketball game originally scheduled for Nov 6, 2026
rules_evidence.establishes: Settled quantity is the sum of three box-score stats for one named game at an 'N+' integer threshold (floor_strike 24.5), so it is a count of a sum, with the date of the original schedule governing the match.

rules_evidence.quote: this Contract resolves to the fair price prior to the opening tip of the game unless the player records the required number
rules_evidence.establishes: Protected variant: a first-half-only appearance is void at the pre-tip fair price unless the strike is already reached, so early exit by injury is not a loss for a Yes holder; the distribution of the settled event conditions on playing past halftime.

rules_evidence.quote: If a player is inactive, or active but never takes the court, the market settles to a fair price. Once a player enters the game the market settles based on the player's combined points, rebounds, and assists recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: The unprotected PRA ladder voids only a non-appearance (fair price); once the player enters, an early injury exit settles on the actual (short) total, so the unprotected lower tail includes early exits while the protected one does not.

variants_and_edge_cases: Protected versus unprotected: both PRA variants now have sampled rules. KXNBAPRA (unprotected) voids at fair price only if the player is inactive or never takes the court and otherwise settles on actual stats; KXNBAPRAPROT also voids a first-half-only appearance. KXNBAPR and KXNBAPA are TITLE_ONLY, so their DNP wording is assumed, not seen.
Early-exit void: a player who plays the first half and is hurt at halftime produces a fair-price settlement rather than No, which removes the lower tail that otherwise exists.
Strike on a half point: floor_strike 24.5 with 'N+' means a total of exactly 24 is No and 25 is Yes; the integer sum of three counts has no push.
Overtime: the sampled rule text does not say overtime statistics are included; box-score totals normally include them, adding 5 minutes to starters in about 6% of games.
Stat corrections after the game by the league's scorer can alter an assist or rebound and flip a boundary result.

Void value is circular for expected-value work: the protected void pays "the fair price prior to the opening tip", a market-derived reference that exists only once the market has been priced, so evaluate P(settles on actual stats) and P(void) separately and treat the void payout as exogenous.

The text does not say whether a starter "enters" at the tip or at the start of the third quarter, and a first-half starter rested for the whole second half in a blowout (not an injury) is void on the literal wording unless the strike was already reached.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official league box score (NBA.com game box score) for points, rebounds and assists; the protected clause uses substitution/play-by-play records to determine first-half entry and second-half entry.

mechanism.summary: A combo prop settles on S = PTS + REB + AST over the minutes the player is on court, so the outcome is the sum of three count processes that share one multiplier (minutes) and one environment (possessions) but compete for the same player-level resources. The chain is: does he play and for how long (a mixture over full-length, blowout-truncated, foul-limited and early-exit scenarios), how many team possessions occur in those minutes, which share of them runs through him as shooter, passer or rebounder, how efficiently each opportunity converts, and how the discrete sum lands relative to a half-point threshold. Components are positively correlated through minutes and pace but negatively through role allocation (a creator who scores more shoots instead of assisting; a perimeter-oriented big rebounds fewer), so the variance of the sum is not the sum of variances. The protected clause removes the early-exit lower tail, while overtime and close games add a right tail. Points carry most of the variance, rebounds the least.

stages.name: Participation and protected-state
stages.description: The first gate is whether the player appears. The unprotected KXNBAPRA rule voids inactive or never-on-court players at fair price and settles on actual stats once the player enters, while the protected contract voids a first-half-only appearance unless the strike is already met. So the probability mass is cut at 'minutes = 0' and at 'exit before the halftime return', and what remains is the participation scenario where the player plays at least a second-half minute. Late scratches (inactive 30 minutes before tip), minute restrictions on return and in-game injuries all shape the cut and arrive from official reports and reporter posts at different times. The sampled protected text voids any first-half-only appearance, so the cut includes second halves a coach rests the player through in a first-half blowout, not only injuries, and it is unclear whether a starter who simply plays the whole first half counts as having entered during it.
stages.distribution: Spike at zero (void) plus a thin early-exit spike; remaining mass is a continuous minutes distribution. Conditional on playing, the probability of an in-game exit is a small hazard per minute, higher for players with recent injuries.

stages.name: Minutes scenario mixture
stages.description: Minutes are not one number: a starter on a team projected to win by 14 faces a high probability of a 26-minute night, in a competitive game he plays 36, and with foul trouble he is clipped at 28 and then returns. The scenarios mix with different weights depending on expected margin, coach rotation habits and bench quality, and each scenario has its own stat rate because garbage-time minutes are low-usage. OT adds a fixed block of minutes in roughly one game in sixteen.
stages.distribution: Multimodal mixture (blowout 22-28, normal 32-38, OT 40+) rather than a normal; sd of minutes for starters about 5 and sharply state-dependent, tail truncated at 48+5k.

stages.name: Opportunity volume per minute
stages.description: Per minute, the player has shot attempts and free-throw trips (usage), rebound chances (position of shots and team missed shots in his zone), and potential assists (touches and passes). These depend on pace of the game and on which teammates share the floor: missing the primary creator raises usage but also changes who receives the passes. Rebound chances depend on both teams' miss rates and the number of bigs on court.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed counts per minute; opportunity totals are roughly negative-binomial with a variance that grows with team pace variability and lineup churn.

stages.name: Conversion and luck
stages.description: Points are a conversion of attempts (efficiency with high short-window noise on threes), rebounds convert chances at a rate dominated by position and opponent miss quality, assists convert potential assists at teammate shooting rate and the scorer's credit behaviour. Of the three, points carry the largest luck variance in a single game and assist conversion depends on whether teammates are hot; rebounds are comparatively stable. These conversion terms are partly independent, which softens the covariance of the sum.
stages.distribution: Points: binomial-like per attempt with extra shooting-luck variance; assists: binomial on potential assists with arena credit noise; rebounds: close to Poisson given chances. Sum of three non-identical overdispersed counts.

stages.name: Joint distribution and threshold
stages.description: The settled event is the sum crossing an integer line, so the covariance between components matters for the tails: minutes and pace give a positive common factor while role-share gives a negative one, and the net sign depends on the player type (a scoring wing versus a point-guard creator versus a centre). A scenario mixture on minutes plus component-specific residuals produces a right-skewed sum whose mass at the line depends on the mean and the sd.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed integer distribution with sd roughly 6-8 for a star at a mean near 30; the cumulative mass at the rung depends on scenario weights, not just the mean.

talent_strength.note: Player-level production rates are the ability layer for each component.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent allowed points/rebounds/assists to position; nba.opp_def_pos exists in the catalog but is not attached to this archetype.

role_personnel.note: Who shares the floor changes shot, pass and rebound opportunities in different directions.

availability_news.note: Own and teammates' status plus in-game exit hazard feed the protected-state cut.

coaching_scheme.note: Rotation and garbage-time pull timing decide the minute scenario weights.

environment.note: Altitude, arena and weather act on a single player-game only through possessions and fatigue, which the pace and rest inputs capture; no separate environmental input would add information for a points+rebounds+assists sum.

game_context_script.note: Spread/total environment drives minutes truncation and team scoring.

efficiency_conversion.note: Scoring and assist conversion with luck regression.

distribution_variance.note: Covariance and marginals produce the sum distribution.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Back-to-back, rest and return-from-injury restrictions shift the minutes scenario weights; the 2026-27 load-management policy remains unquantified (u6).

officiating_rules.note: Crew foul tendency changes free-throw points and foul-trouble minutes; assignment availability in machine-readable form is unverified (u5).

settlement_contract.note: Protected clause, strike construction and stat corrections define the settled quantity.

nba.minutes_scenario_mixture.label: Minutes scenario mixture weights and component rates
nba.minutes_scenario_mixture.mechanism: Minutes are a mixture of regimes (blowout truncation, normal, foul-limited, OT, restricted) whose weights depend on game state and each regime has different per-minute stat rates.
nba.minutes_scenario_mixture.rationale: The existing nba.minutes is a point projection that hides the multimodality; for a threshold sum, P(S>=25) is driven by the weight of the full-minutes regime, not by the mean minutes.
nba.minutes_scenario_mixture.measurement: From 3+ seasons of play-by-play, classify each player-game into regimes by the minutes and score margin (blowout: |margin|>=18 with 4th-quarter minutes<8; foul-limited: >=4 fouls by Q3; OT; restriction: coach-announced); fit regime weights as a multinomial logit of (own-model spread, rest, opponent pace, bench depth) with ridge shrinkage; each regime's stat-per-minute rates estimated with 15-game half-life and a prior from players of the same role; as-of timestamp = last injury report vintage.
nba.minutes_scenario_mixture.why: A PRA rung's probability is dominated by P(full minutes), which the market prices with a single projected minute number.

nba.early_exit_hazard.label: Protected-void probability: first-half-only participation (injury, ejection, illness or coach-rested second half)
nba.early_exit_hazard.mechanism: P(player enters in the first half but never after halftime, including OT) = injury/ejection/illness exit hazard plus the coach decision to rest him for the whole second half in a lopsided game; the protected clause voids both unless the strike was already reached.
nba.early_exit_hazard.rationale: Early exit by injury is only one route to the void state: the sampled protected text voids any player who enters in the first half and does not enter after it, so a starter pulled for the entire second half of a first-half blowout is also void. Both routes are unrelated to per-minute rates and the second is strongly tied to the first-half margin.
nba.early_exit_hazard.measurement: Two components over the last 3 seasons. (a) Injury/ejection/illness exit hazard h = exits (left and did not return) / minutes, shrunk to a position prior with k=2000 minutes and scaled by 1.5 for the first 3 games after a listed injury; P(exit before half) = 1 - exp(-h*minutes_in_half1). (b) Coach-rest route: from play-by-play, P(no second-half entry | played first half and non-injury) by own-model pregame spread bucket and coach, estimated on 3 seasons with beta shrinkage k=30 games; combine as 1-(1-a)(1-b); then convert by contract wording (protected void vs actual stats, with the strike-already-reached carve-out).
nba.early_exit_hazard.why: Protected PRA contracts void on first-half-only participation, which includes coach-rested second halves, so the void probability must be modelled separately from injury status.

nba.lineup_conditional_component_rates.label: Lineup-conditional per-100 rates for points, rebounds and assists
nba.lineup_conditional_component_rates.mechanism: The three components move differently when teammates are on or off court: a creator off court raises the player's usage and assists, a big off court raises rebounds.
nba.lineup_conditional_component_rates.rationale: Season-average per-minute rates blur lineup regimes, and teammate_absence_shift is a single directional signal; separate rates per partner set are needed for a sum that moves in offsetting directions.
nba.lineup_conditional_component_rates.measurement: Per player: per-100-possession PTS, REB, AST computed by on-court partner set (with/without each of the top-3 teammates by minutes), minimum 300 possessions per cell, empirical-Bayes shrinkage toward the player's overall rate with k=400 possessions; applied to tonight's expected lineup from the confirmed or projected starters; as-of = latest lineup information.
nba.lineup_conditional_component_rates.why: A 'missing teammate' flag cannot tell whether PRA rises (scoring/assist boost) or just redistributes (points up, assists down).

nba.own_game_environment.label: Own-model game environment (team points, possessions)
nba.own_game_environment.mechanism: Both teams' scoring environment determines how many scoring chances exist in the minutes played.
nba.own_game_environment.rationale: nba.implied_team_totals is derived from the sportsbook spread and total, which is market-derived, so it should be a benchmark; an own estimate from ratings and pace gives an independent environment.
nba.own_game_environment.measurement: Team points = pace_own x (opponent-adjusted ORtg) / 100 using 20-game exponentially weighted ratings with opponent adjustment by ridge (lambda tuned on 2 prior seasons); possessions = geometric mean of the two teams' opponent-adjusted pace; adjustment for tonight's active set via lineup rating deltas; output team points and sd.
nba.own_game_environment.why: The environment is needed independent of the market price; using spread-implied points would make the model a function of its own benchmark.

nba.load_mgmt.label: Load management / return-from-injury minutes restrictions
nba.load_mgmt.mechanism: Teams rest stars on back-to-backs, in lopsided situations and when returning from injury with announced minute limits, reducing minutes unpredictably.
nba.load_mgmt.rationale: Load management is a policy: age, injury history, rest rules (e.g. no consecutive-night games for certain players), and clinching status predict absences and minute caps. Returning players typically have restrictions (e.g. 20-24 minutes) that are first announced or reported on game day, so a pregame model must carry a probability. Subtle: the NBA's player participation policies and 65-game award eligibility alter incentives.
nba.load_mgmt.measurement: Player-level: games missed on back-to-backs vs non-b2b, age, prior-season availability, injury return flags, games since return, restrictions reported; team-level policy tendency; probability of rest by day-of-week and rest status.
free_sources: NBA official injury report PDF (official.nba.com, free; updates through the day before and day of game)
Spotrac / RealGM / Pro Sports Transactions (free tiers: contracts, cap, transactions)
nba.load_mgmt.why: Return-from-injury minute restrictions and coach-announced rest set the restriction branch of the minutes mixture; the record's own minutes mixture lists a coach-announced restriction regime that needs this input.

nba.rest_travel.label: Rest, back-to-back, travel, altitude
nba.rest_travel.mechanism: Fatigue from short rest, back-to-backs and dense schedule modestly lowers efficiency and, through coaching decisions, changes minutes and availability.
nba.rest_travel.rationale: Rest effects on team performance are small but real; larger is the indirect channel where stars sit on the second night of a back-to-back, which is handled by availability inputs. Rest differential (not absolute rest) matters for the spread; 3-in-4 and 4-in-6 clusters, and games after long road trips, add tail risk. Subtle: effect sizes have shrunk in the sports-science era and must be fit on recent seasons only.
nba.rest_travel.measurement: Per team: days of rest, is_b2b, second_game_of_b2b_on_road, games in last 4/6/7 days, rest differential; interactions with age and minutes load; fit effect on margin residual vs closing line.
nba.rest_travel.why: Back-to-back, rest days and travel change star minutes and the probability of load-managed rest; shifts the weights of the minutes scenarios.

nba.referee_crew.label: Referee crew tendencies (fouls, pace, total, home bias)
nba.referee_crew.mechanism: The assigned crew's foul-calling rate sets free-throw volume, foul trouble, and game pace, affecting totals and certain player props.
nba.referee_crew.rationale: Crew assignments are public the morning of game day, so they are knowable but the effect is modest and the historical estimate noisy; crews with higher foul rates raise free-throw attempts and lower fluidity. Subtle: crew effects are partly confounded by the teams they officiated; need to regress crew effect on fouls/total residual controlling for teams.
nba.referee_crew.measurement: Mixed-effects model: total or FTA residual ~ crew chief + referees + team effects with shrinkage; rolling 2-3 seasons; compute expected fouls/FTA shift for tonight's crew.
free_sources: NBA official referee assignments (official.nba.com, free, posted morning of game day)
NBA Last Two Minute reports (official.nba.com, free)
Basketball-Reference (free; polite scraping, rate-limited) game box scores list officials
nba.referee_crew.why: Crew foul tendency changes free-throw points, foul trouble (minutes clipped) and pace; used only as a secondary driver of the points and minutes components.

nba.scorer_bias.label: Official scorer/arena stat-credit bias (assists, steals, blocks, rebounds)
nba.scorer_bias.mechanism: Statistics like assists, blocks and steals are subjective official-scorer judgments, and arena-level tendencies (home scorer) can shift counts systematically.
nba.scorer_bias.rationale: If home arenas credit more assists/blocks/steals to the home team, prop outcomes depend on venue and the scorer culture; the effect can be measured as arena-level residual in stat/min controlling for team and opponent. It is a hypothesis, probably small, and needs panel data over multiple seasons. Subtle: team-composition confounds (a team always plays at its own arena), so use opponent-team residuals at the same venue.
nba.scorer_bias.measurement: Mixed-effects model of assists/blocks/steals per 100 possessions with team-offense, team-defense and venue random effects; arena effect = home-arena random effect on both teams.
free_sources: Basketball-Reference (free; polite scraping, rate-limited) team game logs by arena
hoopR / sportsdataverse (free R/Python pull of ESPN and NBA data)
nba.scorer_bias.why: Official-scorer and arena credit bias moves assists, and to a lesser extent rebounds, at the boundary of a three-stat sum; referenced in stage s4 and now attached.

nba.teammate_conv.label: Teammate shot conversion / shooting quality
nba.teammate_conv.mechanism: Assists depend on whether the shots a player creates are made; the shooting skill and shot quality of teammates on the floor raises or lowers conversion.
nba.teammate_conv.rationale: Teammate expected eFG on the passes created (shooters like catch-and-shoot specialists vs low-percentage players) changes assists per potential assist from ~0.4 to ~0.6. Subtle: conversion has luck (hot/cold shooters) that should be regressed, but real roster quality changes (star shooter returning or leaving) is real signal.
nba.teammate_conv.measurement: AST/potential assist history; expected conversion = sum over teammates of pass share x teammate expected eFG given shot type; use shrinkage; condition on which teammates are active tonight.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) shotchartdetail, leaguedashptstats (Passing: by teammate)
PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)
raw_data: assisted field goals by passer-shooter pair
nba.teammate_conv.why: Teammates' conversion of the player's passes sets assists per potential assist; referenced in stage s4 and coverage and now attached.

nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.label: Ratings-based blowout probability and starter-minutes-vs-margin curve (market-free)
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.mechanism: Rebuilds the blowout risk from team strength and rotation history instead of the closing spread: a ratings-implied expected margin and margin spread give P(large lead), and a coach/player minutes-versus-margin curve converts each margin path into expected minutes lost by starters and gained by bench players.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.rationale: The catalog input nba.garbage is defined from the closing spread, which is a market price and so a benchmark, not an input. The causal quantity is the chance that the margin passes the coach's pull threshold early enough to matter, and how much playing time each player then loses. Subtle: the loss depends on when the lead arrives (a 20-point lead entering Q4 removes far more starter minutes than one reached with 3 minutes left), on the coach, and on whether the trailing team also pulls starters, so the curve must be conditional on the margin path and not only on the final margin.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.measurement: Step 1, expected margin: mu = (NetRtg_home_adj - NetRtg_away_adj) * expected_possessions/100 + home_adv, where NetRtg_adj is the as-of-tipoff opponent-adjusted net rating from nba.off_rtg and nba.def_rtg (ridge regression on game point differential, half-life about 25 games, shrunk to the preseason prior with n_prior about 20 games as a placeholder to be fitted), adjusted for the confirmed unavailable players via nba.lineup_adj_rating, home_adv fitted on the last 5 seasons (about 2 points). Step 2, margin spread: sd_margin fitted on 5 seasons of residuals of final margin versus mu (league-wide roughly 12-13 points, to be estimated, with a heavier empirical tail than normal). Step 3: P(final |margin| >= 15/20/25) and P(|lead| >= 15/20 entering Q4) from the empirical residual distribution around mu. Step 4, minutes curve: from play-by-play stints, per team-season, expected minutes of each rotation player conditional on margin entering Q4 in bins (0-9, 10-14, 15-19, 20+), shrunk toward the league curve with k about 30 blowout games. Output per player: expected minutes lost and the probability of falling below a stated minutes level. No closing line or other price is used; the spread is retained only to benchmark calibration of step 3.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com leaguegamelog (team game logs, free, undocumented, rate-limited)
cdn.nba.com liveData playbyplay JSON (substitutions with score, free, unofficial)
Basketball-Reference game logs and play-by-play (free, polite scraping)
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.why: Replaces the spread-based nba.garbage in combo_props: blowout truncation of the relevant players' minutes from own ratings and the coach's pull curve, with no closing line used.
raw_data: team-game final margins and opponent-adjusted ratings as of tipoff (5 seasons)
play-by-play substitution stints with margin entering Q4 (per team-season)

nba.minutes.reason: A single projected minute figure hides the multimodal truncation that drives the sum's tails; keep as a summary but replace the driver with a scenario mixture.

nba.usage.reason: Usage is the right opportunity measure for points, but a usage rate says nothing about assist or rebound components, so it is only one third of the volume story.

nba.combo_covariance.reason: Directly targets the key mechanism (covariance of components) but needs to be conditional on role type and minutes regime; a single covariance matrix per player over-states the minutes-driven part.

nba.stat_dist.reason: Marginal count distributions are needed for the sum convolution; overlaps with combo_covariance in intent so should be fitted jointly, not separately.

nba.teammate_absence_shift.reason: Redistribution is real but different per component; the coarse with/without delta needs the lineup-conditional rates to say which component moves.

nba.reb_chances.reason: Rebound chances give a stable opportunity measure for one component; contested versus uncontested share needs tracking data that is not free.

nba.pot_ast.reason: Potential assists are the opportunity measure for assists; available from tracking, so access is the limit.

nba.shot_profile.reason: Shot location decides points per attempt and rebound location; useful for scoring efficiency, minor for assists.

nba.garbage.reason: Catalog definition is 'Blowout / garbage-time probability from spread' (measurement: P(final |margin| > 15/20/25) as a function of the closing spread), so as defined it is market-derived and only a calibration benchmark; the blowout-minutes mechanism is carried by the market-free nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve (ratings-implied margin plus coach minutes-versus-margin curve).

nba.pace.reason: Pace scales possessions for all three components; overlaps with implied team totals in what it carries.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Status vintage of the player and teammates sets availability and who is on the floor; timing relative to quote time is crucial.

nba.implied_team_totals.reason: Derived from sportsbook spread and total, so market-derived; keep it as a comparison against the own-model environment rather than as a model input.

nba.stat_corrections.reason: A post-game correction can flip a boundary integer in a three-stat sum, so it matters mainly for settlement labels and not for pregame probability.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price path for the three-stat PRA contract; useful to see when information was absorbed and for calibration labels, but it is an observation of the market, never an explanatory driver of the outcome.

m.rules_text.reason: Versioned rules text defines the settled quantity for the three-stat PRA contract; wording changes between series are the only way to know the target variable, so it is a required contract input, not a feature.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook PRA lines are the strongest prior but they are market prices; use only as the benchmark and measure disagreement.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Cross-rung monotonicity of the three-stat PRA contract is derived from Kalshi prices, so it flags stale quotes (an execution diagnostic) and carries no information about the underlying result.

m.strike_hit_rates.reason: Realised frequency by rung for the three-stat PRA contract is a calibration label set rather than a driver; thin samples per rung limit its use.

nba.market_calibration_bias.reason: Price-bucket miscalibration for the three-stat PRA contract is measured on Kalshi prices, so it is a market-derived correction layer applied after a probability exists, not an input.

m.volume_oi.reason: Volume/open interest for the three-stat PRA contract measures liquidity and attention; market-derived and not a driver of the outcome, usable only to discount thin quotes.

m.trade_tape.reason: Trade prints for the three-stat PRA contract are market microstructure; informed-flow inference from them is speculative and cannot be a causal input.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Settled value and timestamp for the three-stat PRA contract are labels for calibration and need reconciling against the named source; not a pregame input.

interactions.mechanism: Expected opportunities are the product of minutes and per-minute volume, but the usage rate itself is lower in garbage minutes, so the product within the blowout regime is much smaller than average minutes times average usage.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate regime-specific usage and compare predicted sums with the naive product on historical games stratified by final margin.

interactions.mechanism: With the primary creator off court, points and assists move in opposite directions for the scorer-passer while points and rebounds move together for a big, so the covariance sign by component pair flips with the lineup.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute component correlations in on/off splits and test whether the sd of the sum differs from the pooled estimate.

interactions.mechanism: Past a expected margin of about 10 points the probability of a truncated-minutes game rises steeply, creating a regime switch in the upper rungs while the lower rungs barely move.
interactions.how_to_test: Bucket own-model expected margin and measure P(S>=strike) by rung across expected margin buckets; look for a knee near 9-12 points.

interactions.mechanism: A questionable teammate's resolution changes the player's usage and assists, and since the protected clause treats the player's own exit separately, the sequence of reports matters: the teammate's status effect is conditional on the player's status being active.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare PRA outcomes by teammate status vintage (listed out before 5pm vs after) controlling for own minutes.

interactions.mechanism: A protected contract voids a first-half exit, so P(Yes | not void) is a conditional on survival to the second half, shifting probability up for high-hazard players relative to the unprotected equivalent.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised hit rates of protected versus unprotected series once voided contracts are removed.

nonlinearities.shape: Knee at |expected margin| near 10, concave beyond
nonlinearities.why: Minutes loss rises slowly for small expected margins and then accelerates as the favourite pulls starters, so the effect on a high rung is convex in the expected margin up to the knee and then saturates.

nonlinearities.shape: Non-Gaussian multimodal with an OT spike
nonlinearities.why: Minutes in the three regimes are 24, 35 and 42 rather than one bell curve; the sum's upper tail is generated mainly by the OT/competitive regime.

nonlinearities.shape: Diminishing returns in points per extra shot
nonlinearities.why: Higher usage reduces efficiency, so doubling shot share does not double points, which flattens the points component for stars.

nonlinearities.shape: Right-skewed integer sum with overdispersion
nonlinearities.why: Count components are overdispersed; the three-component sum has a heavier right tail than a normal with the same sd.
