nba.game_pace_composition.label: Game-pace composition rule from two teams' tempos
nba.game_pace_composition.mechanism: Expected game possessions as a function of both teams' pace, transition frequency and turnover rates rather than a simple average.
nba.game_pace_composition.rationale: The draft states that the slower team controls tempo; the empirical rule must be fitted, with transition frequency and defence-forced turnovers as additional terms.
nba.game_pace_composition.measurement: Regress game possessions on (paceA + paceB)/2, |paceA - paceB|, each team's transition-frequency and turnover rate and rest, using 5 seasons of team-games with opponent-adjusted paces (20-game half-life); report coefficients and residual sd; as-of the last completed game; adjust for active set via nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decomposition.
nba.game_pace_composition.why: Total is multiplicative in possessions, so a 2-possession error shifts the mean total by about 4 points.

nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decompositio.label: Absence effect split into pace and efficiency components
nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decompositio.mechanism: Each rotation player's absence changes team pace and ORtg/DRtg separately, with different signs by role.
nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decompositio.rationale: The existing lineup_adj_rating collapses availability into one net rating, which is the right variable for margin but wrong for totals where a slower-and-worse offence and a faster-and-weaker defence have opposite effects.
nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decompositio.measurement: For each player with at least 800 minutes: on/off differences in team possessions per 48, ORtg and DRtg over 3 seasons with ridge shrinkage (k=600 possessions) and teammate adjustment (RAPM-style regression on pace as well); apply to tonight's scenario weights; as-of nightly after injury report.
raw_data: lineup stints with possessions and points
nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decompositio.why: The draft's interaction about ball handlers and rim protectors has no measurable input behind it.

nba.three_point_variance_load.label: Three-point attempt volume as a variance load
nba.three_point_variance_load.mechanism: The sd of the total depends on how many threes both teams attempt and on the dispersion of free-throw and two-point results.
nba.three_point_variance_load.rationale: The draft says total sd is about 17-19 as a constant; it varies with shot mix, and wide-open three-heavy teams produce a wider total distribution that matters at ladder tails.
nba.three_point_variance_load.measurement: Var_total = Σ_team [9*3PA*p3(1-p3) + 4*2PA*p2(1-p2) + FTA*pft(1-pft)] + var(possessions)*ppp^2*... using opponent-adjusted attempts and rates (20-game half-life); calibrate a scale factor lambda so that predicted variance matches realised total residual variance in 2 prior seasons; report sd per game and skew.
nba.three_point_variance_load.why: Ladder rungs far from the mean depend on the tail; using a constant sd misprices those rungs.

nba.series_length_distribution.label: Series-length distribution from per-game win probabilities
nba.series_length_distribution.mechanism: The number of games in a best-of-seven series is a function of per-game win probability, home pattern and dependence between games.
nba.series_length_distribution.rationale: KXNBASERIESGAMES counts games, not points; the draft has no input for it except a generic series model reference outside the archetype.
nba.series_length_distribution.measurement: P(series ends in k games) by dynamic programming over home pattern 2-2-1-1-1 with per-game win probabilities from own-model ratings and series dependence parameter (game-to-game correlation about +0.05 on margin, estimated from 2000-2025 playoff series); injuries known as of the as-of date; output P(4), P(5), P(6), P(7).
nba.series_length_distribution.why: Retained only because it was merged from this record for KXNBASERIESGAMES (now in series_and_cup); not used by the points stages here.

nba.series_model.label: Best-of-seven series model (home-court, game-to-game correlation, adjustments)
nba.series_model.mechanism: Series win and game-count probabilities derive from per-game win probabilities with home pattern; correlated injuries and adjustments change the distribution.
nba.series_model.rationale: A simple independent binomial overstates sweeps vs actual; playoff rotations shorten, pace slows, and stars play more minutes, shifting the effective team rating. Series props (sweep, exact games, player series totals) need game-level scoring simulations. Subtle: in-series injuries and coaching adjustments create positive correlation between games.
nba.series_model.measurement: Per-game win p from playoff-adjusted ratings with home advantage; sample game-to-game correlation parameter; adapt rating after injuries; compute pmf of series length and winner.
nba.series_model.why: Retained only because it was merged from this record for KXNBASERIESGAMES, which the reconciliation moved to series_and_cup; it is not used by the points stages here.

nba.summer_league_minutes.label: Summer League rosters, minutes plans and rookie usage
nba.summer_league_minutes.mechanism: Summer League games feature unstable rosters, rookie/two-way minutes plans and shortened rotations, making roles and pace less predictable.
nba.summer_league_minutes.rationale: Teams use Summer League to evaluate young players, often with explicit minute caps or rotations, and lineup announcements arrive late. Subtle: little data per player, and team strength priors are weak; heavy uncertainty and different pace/total behavior than regular season.
nba.summer_league_minutes.measurement: Roster list with draft status/two-way contract, previous-year Summer League usage, announced minutes plans, game-day scratches; league-level pace and scoring baseline for Summer League.
free_sources: NBA Summer League box scores (nba.com, free)
raw_data: Summer League rosters and minute plans
nba.summer_league_minutes.why: Retained only because it was merged from this record for KXNBASUMMERTOTAL, which the reconciliation moved to summer_league_games; it is not used by the points stages here.

nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.label: Own-model regulation tie probability P(OT)
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.mechanism: P(OT) = mass of regulation margin at zero from a heteroscedastic margin density with a late-game excess-mass correction.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.rationale: The draft claims P(OT) is roughly flat across spreads, but a Gaussian with sd 12 gives 3.3% at pick-em and 2.3% at 10 points, so the dependence on spread is large; the right model is a decreasing function with an empirical excess factor.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.measurement: P_gauss(0) = phi(mu/sigma)/sigma with mu own-model margin and sigma from nba.margin sd model (about 12, scale sqrt(possessions)); multiply by excess factor kappa(|mu|) estimated by isotonic regression on 10 seasons of games as observed OT rate divided by P_gauss(0) in |mu| buckets of 2 points; kappa about 1.7-1.9 overall; output with beta interval; use own-model mu, not closing lines. Margin is integer-valued with parity tied to the total, and free-throw, three-point and intentional-foul structure moves mass onto and off zero, so estimate the observed integer pmf at 0 (and smoothed mass at +/-1 to +/-4) over 15 seasons and let kappa(|mu|) absorb the discreteness rather than reading the continuous density at zero.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.why: Market-free probability that regulation ends tied, from the own-model margin mean and sd with an integer-pmf excess at zero; needed because overtime changes the settled quantity.
raw_data: team-game regulation and final scores with period counts (15 seasons)
own-model expected margin and margin sd per game

nba.ot_period_distribution.label: Distribution of number of overtime periods and OT scoring
nba.ot_period_distribution.mechanism: If overtime occurs, additional periods occur with a small probability and each period adds a fixed block of minutes and points.
nba.ot_period_distribution.rationale: The count of OT periods matters for series OT markets and for strike markets on total, bench or team stats within the family; the draft treats OT as one event.
nba.ot_period_distribution.measurement: Empirical P(k OT periods) from 15 seasons: P(1), P(2), P(3+) conditional on OT; per-period points per team sampled from the league distribution adjusted for pace (mean about 11-12 per team per 5 minutes, sd 5); update yearly; for series OT: P(at least one OT game) = sum over series length L of P(L) * (1 - prod over games g of (1 - p_g)), with P(L) from nba.series_model (4-7 games, shorter for mismatched teams) and p_g from nba.reg_tie_pmf_model using each game's own-model margin; inflate the variance across games because closeness is positively correlated within a series (estimate by the observed share of series with >=1 OT game versus the independent prediction on 15 seasons of playoff series). The settled quantity (at least one OT game, or a count) is unsampled, see u6.
nba.ot_period_distribution.why: An overtime period adds roughly a 10-12 point block per team to the total and a second OT adds another, so the OT-count distribution shapes the upper tail of the total.
raw_data: play-by-play period counts and per-period team points (15 seasons)

nba.pace.reason: Possessions are the first multiplicative factor; the entry measures each team's pace but not the two-team composition rule that decides game pace.

nba.off_rtg.reason: For totals offence matters separately from defence; opponent adjustment and shot-luck regression are required.

nba.def_rtg.reason: Defence sets opponent scoring; the draft's remark on shot-luck adjustment is right because opponent 3P% is largely luck.

nba.lineup_adj_rating.reason: It is a net rating (offence minus defence), whereas a total depends on the sum of offences, so net rating confounds a good-offence-bad-defence team with a balanced one.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Report vintage matters, and the role of the missing player (scorer, ball handler, rim protector) decides the sign on the total.

nba.three_pt_luck.reason: Regresses hot three-point shooting, a direct driver of recent totals; effect proportional to 3PA volume.

nba.fouls_ft.reason: Team foul-drawing and free-throw rate for both sides; kept secondary and scoped to the team-level rate only so it does not double count nba.referee_crew (official-level whistle shift after controlling for team rates) or nba.late_game_script (closeness-conditional intentional fouling).

nba.referee_crew.reason: A credible total driver (whistle tendency) but the effect is concentrated in high-FTA games and needs the crew assignment known on game day.

nba.rest_travel.reason: Rest affects efficiency and slightly pace; effect on totals is small compared with ratings and pace.

nba.travel_altitude.reason: The rest_travel definition already lists altitude and travel; listing altitude again repeats the same schedule-environment source.

nba.late_game_script.reason: Intentional fouling in close games adds points to the total; needs an explicit closeness-conditional free-throw point term.

nba.ot_model.reason: Catalog measurement is an empirical P(OT) by |spread| bucket and total bucket, keyed on market lines, so it is a benchmark; the own-model nba.reg_tie_pmf_model supplies P(OT) and nba.ot_period_distribution the points an overtime adds.

nba.score_resid.reason: Total residual 'around lines' is market-centred; the sd should come from own-model volume (nba.three_point_variance_load) rather than a constant of 17-19.

nba.standings_motivation.reason: Relevant mainly through who plays in late-season games; low incremental value if availability inputs are good.

nba.def_scheme.reason: Scheme interacts with shot profile to change points per possession at equal ratings; weak evidence in the regular season.

nba.shot_profile.reason: Three-heavy offences against drop coverages gain; also feeds the variance load.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price path for the full-game total ladder; useful to see when information was absorbed and for calibration labels, but it is an observation of the market, never an explanatory driver of the outcome.

m.rules_text.reason: Versioned rules text defines the settled quantity for the full-game total ladder; wording changes between series are the only way to know the target variable, so it is a required contract input, not a feature.

m.external_lines.reason: The sharp total is the efficient benchmark for the mean; useful for measuring disagreement, not as a model input.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Cross-rung monotonicity of the full-game total ladder is derived from Kalshi prices, so it flags stale quotes (an execution diagnostic) and carries no information about the underlying result.

m.orderbook_depth.reason: Depth and spread on the full-game total ladder set tradable size and minimum edge; they come from the market itself and say nothing about the event mechanism.

nba.market_calibration_bias.reason: Price-bucket miscalibration for the full-game total ladder is measured on Kalshi prices, so it is a market-derived correction layer applied after a probability exists, not an input.

m.volume_oi.reason: Volume/open interest for the full-game total ladder measures liquidity and attention; market-derived and not a driver of the outcome, usable only to discount thin quotes.

m.trade_tape.reason: Trade prints for the full-game total ladder are market microstructure; informed-flow inference from them is speculative and cannot be a causal input.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Settled value and timestamp for the full-game total ladder are labels for calibration and need reconciling against the named source; not a pregame input.

interactions.mechanism: Total equals possessions times combined points per possession, so a fast game between two efficient offences is multiplicatively larger than the sum of separate pace and efficiency effects; the cross term is about 1.5-2 points when both factors are one sd above average.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress total on pace, efficiency and the pace-by-efficiency product across 5 seasons and test the product term.

interactions.mechanism: Missing a primary ball handler lowers pace and efficiency (total falls), while missing a rim protector raises opponent efficiency without changing pace (total rises); the sign depends on the missing role.
interactions.how_to_test: Group games by missing player role and compare residual totals; verify opposite signs.

interactions.mechanism: Crew whistle tendency matters most for teams that live at the line: a high-foul crew adds free-throw points proportional to both teams' free-throw rate, so the crew effect on total is larger when both offences draw many fouls.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact crew foul index with the sum of both teams' FTA rate and test the slope.

interactions.mechanism: A hot three-point streak is more likely to be luck for a high-3PA team (larger noise per game), so regression is heavier for those teams and the variance load is also larger; direction: shrink recent offence more when volume is high.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress next-game total residual on last-10 3P% residual interacted with 3PA rate.

interactions.mechanism: Close games produce both late-fouling free-throw points and OT, so the extra points are positively correlated within the same games; the upper tail of the total is generated by close games more than by high-pace blowouts.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition total residuals on final margin buckets and compare tail mass of high rungs in close vs non-close games.

nonlinearities.shape: Variance increasing in 3PA, sd scales with sqrt(attempts)
nonlinearities.why: The sd of the total rises with the number of threes (9p(1-p) per attempt), so rung probabilities away from the mean are sensitive to shot mix.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold at margin within about 8 points in the last 2 minutes
nonlinearities.why: Intentional fouling begins when a game is within a possession or two; adds 4-10 points only in that state, a switch rather than a slope in the margin.

nonlinearities.shape: Mixture adding a fixed block to the upper tail
nonlinearities.why: The regulation total plus a 24-point OT block in 6% of games creates a bump to the right of the median that a normal misses.

nonlinearities.shape: Sub-linear in the slower team's pace
nonlinearities.why: If the slow team partially controls tempo, game pace responds less than one-for-one to the faster team's tempo, so the average of paces overstates the effect of the fast side.

contract.settlement_definition: KXNBAWINMARGIN, now filed under this key after the reconciliation, settles Yes if the named team wins the named game by a margin inside a closed integer band; the sampled market is 'by 6 to 10 points', settled on the 'official final result' (stated in the postponement clause) with a fair-price void if the game is cancelled or not started within 48 hours. The text never mentions overtime, so overtime inclusion is an inference (a regulation tie has no winner otherwise). Only the 6 to 10 band was observed: the other band edges (1-5, 11-15, 16+ in the ledger example), whether the top band is open-ended, and whether bands are listed for both sides are unverified.

rules_evidence.quote: wins the game by 6 to 10 points in the Brooklyn vs Atlanta Pro Basketball game originally scheduled for Nov 7, 2026
rules_evidence.establishes: The settled quantity is a closed integer band (6 to 10 inclusive) on the named team's winning margin in one game, so a margin of 5 or 11 is No and the named team losing is No.

rules_evidence.quote: the market will remain open and resolve based on the official final result
rules_evidence.establishes: Settlement uses the official final result, stated only in the postponement clause; overtime is not mentioned, so its inclusion in the margin is inferred (a tied game has no winner without it), and a cancelled or long-delayed game resolves to a fair price.

variants_and_edge_cases: Per-side bands: the sampled market names the winning team (Brooklyn by 6 to 10), so each game has a set of mutually exclusive bands for each side whose probabilities must sum to one across both sides.
Closed integer bands (6 to 10 inclusive) mean margins of 5 and 11 fall outside; with NBA integer scores no push or gap exists between adjacent bands.

If overtime counts (inferred from "official final result"), every regulation tie converts into a final margin of typically 1-8 points, adding mass to the lowest band beyond what a smooth density gives; if it did not, a tied regulation score would have no winner, so the inference is strong but unstated.
Postponement within 48 hours still settles on the official final result; beyond that the market voids at fair price.

Whether the highest band is open-ended (16+ or 21+) is unseen; if open-ended, its mass depends on the heavy tail of blowouts and the tail input requirements change (nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve and margin decay dominate).
contract.settlement_data_source: Official final score of the game (league box score); overtime inclusion is inferred from 'official final result', not stated in the sampled rules.

mechanism.summary: A winning-margin band is the probability that the final signed margin falls in a closed integer interval on one side, so the contract is a histogram of one density, not a binary on the mean. The density has four structural features beyond a normal with mean mu and sd sigma: a hole at zero (no ties, so regulation ties move to overtime), a bump at small positive margins from overtime outcomes (final margin after OT is typically 1-8), late-game compression when the trailing team fouls and the leading team keeps the lead at small values, and compression after starters are pulled in blowouts where bench units trim or inflate the margin depending on the second unit's strength. The sum across all bands and both sides must be exactly one, and the middle bands are driven by sigma more than by mu; a band such as 6-10 is the difference of two CDF values, so sigma errors enter directly. The informative inputs are therefore the mean margin from the active-set ratings, the heteroscedastic sd and the empirical shape corrections, in that order.

stages.name: Signed-margin mean and variance
stages.description: The mean of the signed margin comes from the difference of the active-set ratings plus home court, and its sd is about 11-13 and rises with pace and with favourite size. The band probabilities are far more sensitive to sd than win probability is: at mean 6 a one-point change in sd (12 versus 13) moves the 6-10 band by about 1.2 percentage points (16.3% to 15.0%) and P(win) by about 1.4 points, so band probabilities are sensitive to sd but not dramatically more than P(win). The mean uncertainty from questionable players is a mixture that fattens bands on the underdog side.
stages.distribution: Normal body with sd 11-13, heteroscedastic; scenario mixture over star status gives a bimodal signed-margin density before pooling.

stages.name: Final-minutes compression and parity
stages.description: In the last two minutes the trailing team fouls and the leading team shoots free throws, so margins within about 8 points shift toward specific values (a made three moves a 4-point lead to 7, an intentional foul sequence ends at +2 to +6), and a ten-point-plus lead with a minute left is basically fixed. The pmf therefore has spikes and troughs by parity and key numbers (3, 6) that a smooth density does not reproduce. The strength of this effect depends on how often the game is close in the last minutes.
stages.distribution: Non-smooth pmf over margins 1-12 with parity structure; the spikes are about 10-20% relative deviations from the smooth density.

stages.name: Garbage-time margin decay
stages.description: When the lead is large (+15 or more) late in the fourth quarter, coaches pull starters and the bench trades baskets; the final margin is then the margin at the pull time plus a random walk whose drift depends on the relative quality of the two second units and on how early each coach pulls. Leads typically shrink a few points after starters sit, but a deep bench on the leading side can hold or extend the margin. This sets the shape of the 11-15 versus 16+ bands, not the middle bands.
stages.distribution: Margin after the pull: approximately a random walk with sd about 4 points over 6 minutes and drift of -1 to -3 points; strongly dependent on lead size at the time of the pull.

stages.name: Overtime conversion into low bands
stages.description: If the regulation score ties (about 3% from the smooth density and about 6% empirically) a five-minute period is played and the final margin is the OT margin, with a mean absolute value near 5.5 and nearly all outcomes between 1 and 10. This adds roughly 3 percentage points of mass to the 1-5 bands in total that a continuous density would assign elsewhere, and it matters most for bands near zero when the spread is small.
stages.distribution: Tie mass converted into a folded normal with sd about 7 (five minutes of scoring difference); dependence on |spread| through the tie probability.

stages.name: Band construction and coherence
stages.description: The market lists bands for each side, so the model must produce P(A wins by band b) for all bands and both teams and the sum must be one. Because each band is a difference of the CDF at its edges, the cut points near the median of the margin density are sensitive to bias in mu, while the open-ended top band is sensitive to the tail. Rungs priced independently by the market may violate the sum constraint or the unimodality of the density within a side. Coherence is enforced by construction: every band for both sides is integrated from the same own-model integer pmf, so the sum-to-one and unimodality constraints need no input derived from quoted prices (m.ladder_structure is only a benchmark diagnostic of stale quotes).
stages.distribution: Multinomial over 8-10 outcomes with a unimodal-per-side density; sum-to-one constraint couples all bands.

talent_strength.note: Mean signed margin from active-set ratings.

opponent_matchup.note: Scheme clash width and second-unit match-up.

role_personnel.note: Who plays after starters sit decides margin decay.

environment.note: Venue, altitude and travel shift the mean margin by about a point, which is carried by the rating and home-court terms in the moneyline archetype; bands add no independent environmental mechanism.

pace_volume.note: Possessions scale the variance of the margin.

efficiency_conversion.note: Three-point shooting luck regressed to shot quality corrects the rating that sets the margin mean and is a large part of single-game variance; it does not predict individual-game conversion.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Seeding stakes and rest decide starter minutes in lopsided games and whether coaches pull starters early, but no input links the motivation state to pull timing; blowout probability alone does not capture it.

officiating_rules.note: Referee tendencies shift free-throw counts and the late-game foul sequence only marginally, and no evidence ties crew identity to margin bands beyond what pace and fouls already capture.

settlement_contract.note: Closed integer bands, final result and fair-price void are read from the sampled KXNBAWINMARGIN rule; the band set beyond 6 to 10 is unobserved. Band coherence is enforced by construction from one own-model pmf, not from quoted prices.

nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.label: Empirical final-margin pmf by own-model mean and sd
nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.mechanism: The final margin has non-smooth pmf structure (hole at zero, OT bump, late-game parity) that a normal density does not reproduce.
nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.rationale: The draft names score_resid as the margin density by spread bucket, but spread buckets from market lines are circular and the pmf structure lives at the integer level; band edges at 5/6 and 10/11 fall exactly on such structure.
nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.measurement: Collect 15 seasons of final signed margins; standardise z = (margin - mu_own)/sigma_own using own-model mean and sd; estimate the pmf of the integer margin by kernel smoothing of the z-density plus an explicit multiplicative correction per integer margin in [-12, 12] (ridge-shrunk to 1); validate by log-loss of band probabilities in 2 held-out seasons; recompute annually.
nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.why: The market has bands, and the discretisation edges at 5/6, 10/11 coincide with the pmf irregularities.

nba.margin_decay_after_pull.label: Margin decay after starters are pulled (by coach and lead size)
nba.margin_decay_after_pull.mechanism: The final margin equals the margin at the pull time plus a bench-vs-bench drift whose size depends on lead and coach.
nba.margin_decay_after_pull.rationale: Blowout probability alone does not tell how much a 20-point lead at 6:00 shrinks; a coach who pulls starters early gives up points.
nba.margin_decay_after_pull.measurement: From play-by-play: margin at the time both starters of the leading team are out and the final margin; compute mean and sd of the change by lead bucket (10-14, 15-19, 20+) and by coach with 3 seasons of data, shrunk to league with k=8 games; as-of the last completed game; output drift and sd for tonight's coaches.
nba.margin_decay_after_pull.why: 11-15 and 16+ bands depend on the drift after the pull, which no input measures.

nba.second_unit_net_rating_gap.label: Second-unit net rating gap
nba.second_unit_net_rating_gap.mechanism: The bench lineups play most late blowout minutes, so the margin drift is the second unit's net rating difference.
nba.second_unit_net_rating_gap.rationale: Starter-based team ratings say nothing about who wins the last six minutes of a blowout; a deep bench preserves a lead.
nba.second_unit_net_rating_gap.measurement: Net rating of the lineups with at most one top-5 player, per 100 possessions, over the last 40 games with opponent adjustment and shrinkage k=250 possessions; gap = team A second unit minus team B second unit; translate to expected margin drift per 6 minutes = gap × 12/100; as-of rotation as projected.
nba.second_unit_net_rating_gap.why: A blowout winner with a weak bench ends in a lower band than the starters' ratings imply.

nba.ot_final_margin_pmf.label: Final-margin pmf conditional on overtime
nba.ot_final_margin_pmf.mechanism: If regulation ties, the final margin is the margin of a five-minute period (or more), concentrated in 1-8 points.
nba.ot_final_margin_pmf.rationale: Mass of the lowest bands is the sum of a regulation part and an OT part; the OT part follows a different distribution with folded structure.
nba.ot_final_margin_pmf.measurement: Empirical pmf of |final margin| for games with OT_periods = 1, 2, 3+ over 15 seasons; fit folded-normal with sd s_OT estimated by maximum likelihood (about 6-7 for one OT); combine with P(OT) from the tie model: P(band) = P(reg in band)(1-P(OT)) + P(OT) × P(OT margin in band).
nba.ot_final_margin_pmf.why: Lowest bands (1-5) get a sizeable share from OT that a Gaussian misses.

nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.label: Pace- and total-dependent margin standard deviation (own-model, not line-based)
nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.mechanism: Margin variance scales with possession count and total scoring, and with spread through garbage time.
nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.rationale: The existing score_resid is defined around lines, which is market-derived; the variance should come from the game's own pace/total estimates so that cover probabilities at wide spreads are correct.
nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.measurement: Fit sd_margin = a + b × sqrt(own-model possessions) + c × |own-model mean margin| on 5 seasons of team-games (own predictions, not closing lines); report quantile curves (10/25/50/75/90) with a skew parameter for heavy favourites; validate by the probability integral transform per bucket.
nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.why: Margin sd (own-model, pace- and spread-dependent) is the main driver of middle-band probabilities and replaces the WEAK market-line nba.score_resid.

nba.three_pt_luck.label: Team three-point shooting luck vs shot quality (own and opponent)
nba.three_pt_luck.mechanism: Realized team 3P% regresses toward a shot-quality-based expectation; opponent 3P% allowed is mostly outside the defense's control on open looks.
nba.three_pt_luck.rationale: Hot or cold shooting streaks inflate or deflate recent offensive/defensive ratings and totals; ignoring regression overstates how hot teams will score and how stingy lucky defenses are. Subtle: shooters' true skill still differs, so expectation must use shooter-specific priors and shot openness, not a league mean.
nba.three_pt_luck.measurement: Expected 3P% = sum over attempts of shooter prior (career/regressed) adjusted for openness; luck = actual - expected over trailing N games; estimate shrinkage factor from out-of-sample reversion; same for opponent 3P% allowed with league-mean prior weighted heavily.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) shotchartdetail, leaguedashteamshotlocations; synergy
PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)
raw_data: team and opponent 3P% vs shot quality
nba.three_pt_luck.why: Three-point shooting luck is a large share of single-game margin variance and of the regression of team rating; it is a rating-correction input here, not a band driver by itself.

nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.label: Ratings-based blowout probability and starter-minutes-vs-margin curve (market-free)
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.mechanism: Rebuilds the blowout risk from team strength and rotation history instead of the closing spread: a ratings-implied expected margin and margin spread give P(large lead), and a coach/player minutes-versus-margin curve converts each margin path into expected minutes lost by starters and gained by bench players.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.rationale: The catalog input nba.garbage is defined from the closing spread, which is a market price and so a benchmark, not an input. The causal quantity is the chance that the margin passes the coach's pull threshold early enough to matter, and how much playing time each player then loses. Subtle: the loss depends on when the lead arrives (a 20-point lead entering Q4 removes far more starter minutes than one reached with 3 minutes left), on the coach, and on whether the trailing team also pulls starters, so the curve must be conditional on the margin path and not only on the final margin.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.measurement: Step 1, expected margin: mu = (NetRtg_home_adj - NetRtg_away_adj) * expected_possessions/100 + home_adv, where NetRtg_adj is the as-of-tipoff opponent-adjusted net rating from nba.off_rtg and nba.def_rtg (ridge regression on game point differential, half-life about 25 games, shrunk to the preseason prior with n_prior about 20 games as a placeholder to be fitted), adjusted for the confirmed unavailable players via nba.lineup_adj_rating, home_adv fitted on the last 5 seasons (about 2 points). Step 2, margin spread: sd_margin fitted on 5 seasons of residuals of final margin versus mu (league-wide roughly 12-13 points, to be estimated, with a heavier empirical tail than normal). Step 3: P(final |margin| >= 15/20/25) and P(|lead| >= 15/20 entering Q4) from the empirical residual distribution around mu. Step 4, minutes curve: from play-by-play stints, per team-season, expected minutes of each rotation player conditional on margin entering Q4 in bins (0-9, 10-14, 15-19, 20+), shrunk toward the league curve with k about 30 blowout games. Output per player: expected minutes lost and the probability of falling below a stated minutes level. No closing line or other price is used; the spread is retained only to benchmark calibration of step 3.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com leaguegamelog (team game logs, free, undocumented, rate-limited)
cdn.nba.com liveData playbyplay JSON (substitutions with score, free, unofficial)
Basketball-Reference game logs and play-by-play (free, polite scraping)
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.why: Replaces the spread-based nba.garbage in game_win_margin: blowout truncation of the relevant players' minutes from own ratings and the coach's pull curve, with no closing line used.
raw_data: team-game final margins and opponent-adjusted ratings as of tipoff (5 seasons)
play-by-play substitution stints with margin entering Q4 (per team-season)

nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.label: Own-model regulation tie probability P(OT)
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.mechanism: P(OT) = mass of regulation margin at zero from a heteroscedastic margin density with a late-game excess-mass correction.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.rationale: The draft claims P(OT) is roughly flat across spreads, but a Gaussian with sd 12 gives 3.3% at pick-em and 2.3% at 10 points, so the dependence on spread is large; the right model is a decreasing function with an empirical excess factor.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.measurement: P_gauss(0) = phi(mu/sigma)/sigma with mu own-model margin and sigma from nba.margin sd model (about 12, scale sqrt(possessions)); multiply by excess factor kappa(|mu|) estimated by isotonic regression on 10 seasons of games as observed OT rate divided by P_gauss(0) in |mu| buckets of 2 points; kappa about 1.7-1.9 overall; output with beta interval; use own-model mu, not closing lines. Margin is integer-valued with parity tied to the total, and free-throw, three-point and intentional-foul structure moves mass onto and off zero, so estimate the observed integer pmf at 0 (and smoothed mass at +/-1 to +/-4) over 15 seasons and let kappa(|mu|) absorb the discreteness rather than reading the continuous density at zero.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.why: Market-free probability that regulation ends tied, from the own-model margin mean and sd with an integer-pmf excess at zero; needed because overtime changes the settled quantity.
raw_data: team-game regulation and final scores with period counts (15 seasons)
own-model expected margin and margin sd per game

nba.score_resid.reason: Described as the empirical margin density by spread bucket, but spread buckets come from market lines (circular) and it is not tied to the integer band edges that settle this contract.

nba.garbage.reason: Catalog definition is 'Blowout / garbage-time probability from spread' (measurement: P(final |margin| > 15/20/25) as a function of the closing spread), so as defined it is market-derived and only a calibration benchmark; the blowout-minutes mechanism is carried by the market-free nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve (ratings-implied margin plus coach minutes-versus-margin curve).

nba.lineup_adj_rating.reason: Provides the mean signed margin; the band is more sensitive to sd than to this mean, so its precision is not the bottleneck.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: A star in or out moves the mean by several points and creates a bimodal density that fattens bands on both sides.

nba.pace.reason: Pace scales sd of margin (more possessions, more variance), which drives middle-band probabilities; effect on mean is nil.

nba.ot_model.reason: Catalog measurement is an empirical P(OT) by |spread| bucket and total bucket, keyed on market lines, so it is a benchmark; the own-model nba.reg_tie_pmf_model supplies P(OT) and nba.ot_final_margin_pmf the post-OT margin.

nba.late_game_script.reason: Late fouling shifts the pmf at margins 1-8, a real effect, but the draft states it only qualitatively.

nba.off_rtg.reason: Component of the mean margin; offence and defence differ in variance contribution but this is minor for bands.

nba.def_rtg.reason: Component of the mean margin; redundant with lineup_adj_rating for the mean.

nba.rotation.reason: Marked context in the draft but starter pull timing is what controls the upper bands; mislabelled and should be primary for the 11+ bands.

nba.def_scheme.reason: Claims that scheme clashes widen or narrow the margin, but there is little evidence of variance effects beyond pace; the mean effect is already in ratings.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price path for the winning-margin bands; useful to see when information was absorbed and for calibration labels, but it is an observation of the market, never an explanatory driver of the outcome.

m.rules_text.reason: Versioned rules text defines the settled quantity for the winning-margin bands; wording changes between series are the only way to know the target variable, so it is a required contract input, not a feature.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook price for the winning-margin bands is a market-derived quantity; keep as a comparison benchmark to measure disagreement, do not use as an input to the probability model.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Band prices should sum to one across both sides and be unimodal per side; violations flag stale quotes or arbitrage but come from the market, so they cannot be model inputs.

interactions.mechanism: A band probability is a CDF difference (mu-b)/sigma, so errors in sigma and in mu multiply: when the mean is near a band's centre, sigma matters more than mu, but for a band two sds away mu matters more.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute the sensitivity of band probabilities to sigma and mu on a grid and identify where each error dominates.

interactions.mechanism: Once the lead exceeds about 15 with under six minutes left the starters leave and the margin drifts rather than grows; the effect of an extra point of lead on the final margin falls from about one to about 0.5 beyond the threshold.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress final margin on margin at 6:00 with a hinge at 15 and compare slope above and below.

interactions.mechanism: The drift after the pull depends on the second-unit gap: a leading team with the stronger bench keeps its lead, otherwise it shrinks; the sign is conditional on the gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Group blowouts by the second-unit gap tercile and compare mean change of margin after pull.

interactions.mechanism: In the regime where regulation ties (3-6% of games) the final margin follows the folded OT density, which is concentrated in 1-8; the lowest bands are a mixture of regulation and OT regimes and the mixture weight falls with spread.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the mixture with mixture weight as a function of own-model spread and compare log loss against a single density.

interactions.mechanism: In a faster game there are more possessions in the final two minutes, so the late-foul sequences take more time and add margins in 4-8 points; pmf spikes become less pronounced as pace rises.
interactions.how_to_test: Contrast the final-margin pmf at 1-8 points in the top versus bottom pace tercile in close games.

nonlinearities.shape: Slope falls from 1 to about 0.5 beyond a 15-point lead at 6:00
nonlinearities.why: Coaches pull starters when a lead is large; additional lead points are given back by bench play, so the final margin is a concave function of the late margin.

nonlinearities.shape: Non-smooth with parity spikes and a zero hole
nonlinearities.why: Integer margins show relative deviations from a smooth density by up to 10-20% at margins 1-8, which determine band edges at 5/6 and 10/11. The 10-20% size is recalled, not measured (u2).

nonlinearities.shape: Heteroscedastic: sd grows with favourite size and pace
nonlinearities.why: Wider spreads have larger sd (heavy tail of blowouts), so band probabilities on the favourite side spread out more than a constant-sd model implies.

required_data.timestamp_requirement: Final results; use only games before the target game.
Final data.
As-of quote time.

unresolved.description: The size of the OT/parity corrections to the margin pmf is recalled, not measured, and may vary with rule changes (the 2022-23 clutch rules, intentional foul rules).
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Estimate the corrections on the last 10 seasons and test for structural breaks.

unresolved.description: Clean identification of when each team's starters were pulled needs substitution-level data with correct clock parsing; free play-by-play has known timestamp errors.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Audit a sample of pull times by video or buy tracking data.

contract.settlement_definition: Each market resolves Yes only if a specific, officially confirmed off-court event occurs inside a stated window, and the sampled rules define the qualifying stage narrowly: a team sale needs the deal 'finalized and approved by the Governing League', a stake sale needs a signed definitive agreement (closing may come later), a franchise-value market needs a definitive purchase agreement plus approvals and a headline value above the strike, a league announcement needs a firm decision naming a confirmed inaugural season, retirement needs an announcement of intent effective immediately or before the next season, and a rule change needs formal adoption before the 2026-27 regular season. Eastern Time windows are stated only in KXNBAEUROPEANNOUNCE, and "all markets resolve to No" absent the event is stated only in KXNBAFRANCHISECOST and KXNBANEXTGOVERNOR; the same wording for the other series (10 of the 21 series under this key after the reconciliation have sampled rules) is not verified. The reconciliation moved Executive of the Year to awards_draft and the player and game specials to season_stat_markets, and kept the player-transaction markets here: KXNBANEXTTEAM (sampled: a free-agent signing with any team, including the previous one, resolves that team Yes, with a Retires / No Team catch-all), KXNBANEXTTEAMCONF and KXNBANEXTCONTRACT (TITLE_ONLY, contract size), which stages s1 and s3 now cover through the destination and contract-value inputs.

rules_evidence.quote: The deal must be finalized and approved by the Governing League to be encompassed by the Payout Criterion.
rules_evidence.establishes: Team-sale Yes requires league approval, not merely an agreement or a report, so the qualifying stage is the end of the governance pipeline.

rules_evidence.quote: Negotiations, letters of intent, drafts, rumors, and unexecuted or conditional announcements do not count.
rules_evidence.establishes: A stake-sale Yes needs a signed definitive agreement; the earlier stages that reporters cover are explicitly excluded, so reporter signals are only leading indicators.

rules_evidence.quote: Preliminary discussions, negotiations, statements of general intent, and a possible earliest start without a confirmed inaugural season do not qualify.
rules_evidence.establishes: A league announcement must name a confirmed inaugural season; statements of intent do not count, creating a sharp wording threshold.

rules_evidence.quote: Merely selecting a preferred bidder is insufficient.
rules_evidence.establishes: Franchise-value Yes needs a definitive agreement and approvals with the headline value above the strike, and bundled assets are stripped out.

rules_evidence.quote: The retirement must be intended to be effective immediately or prior to the first new season after the announcement.
rules_evidence.establishes: Retirement markets need an announcement with a timing condition, so a vague 'this will be my last year' statement may not satisfy it.

rules_evidence.quote: is a free agent, whether restricted or unrestricted, for any period of time and signs a contract with any team, including their previous team
rules_evidence.establishes: A re-signing after any free-agent spell resolves the previous team Yes, so the destination distribution must include staying via Bird rights as an outcome distinct from remaining under contract.

variants_and_edge_cases: Qualifying stage differs by series: announcement (KXNBAEUROPEANNOUNCE, KXNBARETIRE), definitive agreement (KXNBASTAKESALE), definitive agreement plus all approvals (KXNBAFRANCHISECOST), finalized and approved (KXNBATEAMSALE), or formal adoption (KXNBARULE).
Windows and time zone: announcements must occur after market issuance and before the stated date in Eastern Time, so an event announced late on the closing date can fall on either side.

Exclusions and carve-outs: 'one free throw' rule excludes the last two minutes of the fourth quarter and overtime, the governor market excludes the holder at issuance and any acting or alternate governor, bundled assets are stripped from headline values.

Multi-outcome construction: Next Team and Next Team Conference (KXNBANEXTTEAM, KXNBANEXTTEAMCONF) are mutually exclusive destination sets with a Retires / No Team catch-all, where re-signing after free agency counts as a destination; Next Contract (KXNBANEXTCONTRACT) is a contract-size market whose strike construction (total value or annual value) is unseen.

Eleven of the 21 live series have no sampled rules (trade, pick trade, apology, relocation, stadium, team announce, join conference, players to join CBA, franchise owner, next team conference, next contract), so their qualifying stages are unverified.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official league or team announcements, league-approved transaction records and credible primary reporting where the rule allows; no single stat feed.

mechanism.summary: Off-court events are sparse, one-off outcomes generated by organisations, so the mechanism is a process of stage-gated progress against a deadline rather than a rate per opportunity. An event happens when (1) it is feasible under league rules and finances (salary cap and apron constraints for trades, board-of-governors approval for sales and relocations, expansion process), (2) a decision-maker with incentives chooses to pursue it (an owner's liquidity and valuation, a front office's competitive position, a player's career horizon), (3) counterparties agree and the process clears its approval stages, each with typical durations, and (4) a qualifying public act occurs inside the window and at the stage the contract wording requires (announcement, signed definitive agreement, completed approval). Information arrives through reporters whose reliability varies by outlet and by stage, so the key variable is not the rumor but the stage reached and the historical time from that stage to the qualifying act. Hazards are not uniform: they spike around calendar landmarks (draft, free agency, trade deadline, Board meetings).

stages.name: Feasibility under league rules and finances
stages.description: Whether an event can happen at all is governed by hard constraints: trade salary matching tied to payroll tiers (the apron levels), roster size, moratorium dates, the league approval requirement for sales and relocation, the expansion process and the CBA rules for contract extensions. An infeasible event has probability near zero regardless of rumors, and a feasible event has a conditional probability given the actors' incentives; the two are multiplied. For player-transaction markets feasibility is the cap arithmetic: which teams have space or matching salary for the player (nba.player_move_destination_model) and what contract value the maximum and minimum tiers allow (nba.next_contract_value_model), which bounds both the destination set and a contract-size strike.
stages.distribution: Binary feasibility gate times a continuous incentive term; feasibility is deterministic given payroll and roster data and is often the cleanest source of low probabilities.

stages.name: Actor incentive and hazard rate
stages.description: Given feasibility, the decision-maker's incentive determines the base hazard: a coach on a team far below preseason expectation, an owner facing a large capital need, a veteran player approaching the end of a contract all have elevated hazards. The base hazard is estimated from reference classes (how often coaches are fired in a given record-vs-expectation bucket, how often franchises sell) and then updated by org-specific facts.
stages.distribution: Low-rate hazard process, over-dispersed across organisations; discrete events with heavy clustering around specific calendar points.

stages.name: Deal stage progression and approval pipeline
stages.description: Sales, trades and expansions move through ordered stages (exploration, exclusivity, definitive agreement, governance approval, closing), each with a stage-specific completion probability and a typical delay. Because the contracts require a specific stage, the probability is a product of stage-transition probabilities and a timing test against the window. Governance approvals are scheduled around the league's board meetings, which makes approval timing discrete. Rule adoption follows its own committee and Board-of-Governors pipeline and a franchise-value strike needs a valuation model from comparable transactions, not only the event base rate.
stages.distribution: Sequential Bernoulli transitions with log-normal durations between stages; the final-stage timing is clustered around meeting dates.

stages.name: Information flow and reporter reliability
stages.description: The market learns about the stage through reporters and official channels with different lead times and error rates; a report that a deal is 'agreed' from a top-tier reporter has a very high completion rate while 'in talks' reports often fail. The edge is in assigning the right probability to a report given its stage and source, and in timing relative to the official announcement.
stages.distribution: Report-to-event conversion probabilities vary from about 0.1 for 'talks' to over 0.95 for 'agreed' from a tier-one source; lead times of minutes to months.

stages.name: Wording and qualifying-act mapping
stages.description: The final stage is semantic: each contract's wording defines which observable counts (announcement, signed agreement, completed approval, formal adoption). Events can occur in an unrecognised form (a leak, an agreement in principle, a conditional announcement) and fail the wording, or occur on the edge of the window in Eastern Time. The mapping from real-world events to the contract's qualifying act is a model component in itself.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given wording but uncertain because real-world events are ambiguous; mass concentrated at the boundary of the window.

talent_strength.note: Team and player talent matter here only as drivers of incentives (coach firing, retirement); there is no performance measure that directly produces a transaction or announcement, so the performance link is handled as incentive, not strength.

opponent_matchup.note: No head-to-head or opponent-specific process exists for transactions, sales or announcements; counterparty feasibility is handled in the deal pipeline and rule-check inputs, not as a matchup.

role_personnel.note: Decision-makers (owner, GM, coach, player) and their tenure or career stage.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach tendencies in tactics do not produce off-court events; coach-change hazard is a function of record and organisational stability, covered by nba.org_stability.

environment.note: Venue and weather do not drive league approvals or announcements; stadium completion is the only physical-environment contract and its timeline is project-schedule driven, listed as unresolved.

game_context_script.note: These markets have no game script; the relevant timeline is the calendar and deal stage, which sit under situational and settlement categories.

pace_volume.note: There is no count of opportunities to scale; the equivalent is the number of live negotiations or candidate trades, folded into base rates in nba.offfield_base_rate.

efficiency_conversion.note: Conversion of reports to events and of agreements to approvals.

distribution_variance.note: Rare-event base rates and clustered timing.

officiating_rules.note: CBA and league governance rules as the rule layer.

settlement_contract.note: Stage required, window, time zone and carve-outs per series.

nba.governance_approval_pipeline.label: Deal-stage ledger and league approval pipeline
nba.governance_approval_pipeline.mechanism: Sales, relocations and expansions pass through stages (exploration, exclusivity, definitive agreement, governance vote, closing) with stage-specific completion odds and delays.
nba.governance_approval_pipeline.rationale: A rumor-level input cannot tell whether a deal is two weeks or five months from the qualifying stage, and the contracts require specific stages; the pipeline gives P(complete by date).
nba.governance_approval_pipeline.measurement: For each live deal record stage, date entered, and the historical distribution of days to the next stage from past NBA and other major-league sales (log-normal fit per stage, shrunk to cross-league pooled values with k=3 deals); compute P(reach required stage by T) = Π P(transition) × P(duration sum <= T-t); update when a stage is entered; attach the league approval vote threshold as a feasibility gate (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for the exact threshold).
nba.governance_approval_pipeline.why: Sale, stake-sale and franchise-value series require definitive agreement or approval, not rumor, and timing relative to the window is the question.

nba.reporter_reliability_score.label: Reporter and source reliability by report stage
nba.reporter_reliability_score.mechanism: Conversion probability of a report into the qualifying event depends on the reporter and the claim stage (talks, agreed in principle, finalising).
nba.reporter_reliability_score.rationale: The draft input 'transactions, trades, coaching news' is a feed, not a probability; the value is a calibration table P(event | source, stage).
nba.reporter_reliability_score.measurement: Compile reports from tier-one national reporters and team beat writers over 5 seasons, label each with stage (talks / agreed / done), compute completion rate and median lead time to the official act per source and stage with beta-binomial shrinkage k=10 reports; apply to tonight's reports with time decay half-life 7 days for 'talks'; as-of report timestamp.
nba.reporter_reliability_score.why: Prices on trade and signing events should move by the conversion rate of the specific report, which this table supplies.

nba.calendar_hazard_profile.label: Calendar hazard profile (deadlines, draft, free agency, board meetings)
nba.calendar_hazard_profile.mechanism: Event hazard varies with landmarks: trade deadline, draft week, free-agency opening, league board meetings, season start.
nba.calendar_hazard_profile.rationale: A uniform hazard over the window badly misprices markets with a deadline; most transactions cluster in a few days and the remaining hazard collapses after each landmark.
nba.calendar_hazard_profile.measurement: Estimate discrete-time hazard by day-of-year landmark offset from 15 seasons of transactions (trades, coach changes, retirements, signings) with kernel smoothing and a landmark dummy set; P(event in remaining window) = 1 - Π(1-h_d) with hazards conditioned on the event not having occurred; incorporate announced meeting dates as known spikes.
nba.calendar_hazard_profile.why: Deadline-driven markets have a convex hazard; the probability after the trade deadline passes drops to near zero for trades.

nba.qualifying_stage_requirement.label: Qualifying-stage requirement per contract wording
nba.qualifying_stage_requirement.mechanism: Each series names which stage counts; a map from wording to stage lets the model score the right stage.
nba.qualifying_stage_requirement.rationale: The draft treats the wording as a text input, but the useful object is a coded stage per series and the exclusions list, so the same news can be mapped to Yes/No consistently.
nba.qualifying_stage_requirement.measurement: For each series code: required stage (announce / signed definitive / approved / adopted), time zone, window end, carve-outs and multi-outcome rules; fill from rules_primary and rules_secondary of every live series (22 here), mark TITLE_ONLY where no text; test with 20 historical events whether the wording would have resolved Yes.
nba.qualifying_stage_requirement.why: Fifteen of 22 series lack sampled text and the qualifying stage differs among those with text.

nba.career_horizon_signals.label: Player career-horizon signals (age, contract years, injury, public statements)
nba.career_horizon_signals.mechanism: Retirement and next-contract markets depend on age, contract expiry, injury burden, role decline and public statements.
nba.career_horizon_signals.rationale: The draft input injury_risk_season is a season games-missed expectation, not a career-horizon hazard; retirement hazard rises with age and with specific signals such as a farewell tour announcement.
nba.career_horizon_signals.measurement: Per player: age, years remaining on contract, cumulative games missed over last two seasons, minutes trend, explicit retirement statements (coded 0/1/2 by explicitness), compute discrete hazard by age from historical retirements (e.g. age 38+ about 20-25% per year, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED) and multiply by an odds factor for explicit statements; effective date constraint from rule wording.
nba.career_horizon_signals.why: KXNBARETIRE and KXNBANEXTCONTRACT are player decisions governed by horizon signals that the catalog does not capture.

nba.player_move_destination_model.label: Player destination choice model with cap feasibility
nba.player_move_destination_model.mechanism: Destination is a choice among feasible teams determined by cap space or matching assets, team need, and player preference.
nba.player_move_destination_model.rationale: A multi-outcome next-team market needs a distribution over teams; relying on rumor misses cap constraints that exclude most teams.
nba.player_move_destination_model.measurement: For each candidate team compute feasibility (cap space or matching salaries within apron rules), asset fit and need (position gap, win-now vs rebuild); estimate a multinomial logit on 10 seasons of moves with these features plus player-preference flags (stated preference, agent reports); add a catch-all with probability from age and contract status; as-of nightly.
raw_data: team payroll and cap state, historical moves
nba.player_move_destination_model.why: KXNBANEXTTEAM and KXNBANEXTTEAMCONF are filed under this key after the reconciliation and settle on the player's next team (or conference), so a feasibility-constrained destination distribution is the core input.

nba.rule_change_pipeline.label: Rule-change adoption pipeline (competition committee, Board of Governors vote calendar, trial history)
nba.rule_change_pipeline.mechanism: A rule change is adopted only after a proposal clears the competition committee and a Board of Governors vote at a scheduled meeting before the market window ends, so probability is the product of stage-transition rates and a calendar test.
nba.rule_change_pipeline.rationale: KXNBARULE (the "one free throw" rule adopted before the 2026-27 regular season) needs the committee and Board-of-Governors process, the meeting calendar and the history of proposals that were discussed but never adopted; the pooled off-field base rate says nothing about it.
nba.rule_change_pipeline.measurement: Build the list of publicly reported rule proposals 2000-2026 with stage reached (reported idea, committee discussion, committee recommendation, Board vote, adopted) and months from stage to adoption; P(adopt before date) = P(next stage cleared) x ... along the remaining stages x indicator that a scheduled Board meeting falls before the deadline; shrink stage rates toward the all-proposal rate with k=10 proposals; approval threshold (recalled as a three-quarters majority) SOURCE_UNVERIFIED.
free_sources: NBA Board of Governors meeting releases
nba.rule_change_pipeline.why: KXNBARULE depends on a formal adoption pipeline and meeting calendar that no existing input measures.

nba.franchise_valuation_comps.label: Franchise valuation reference class (comparable sale and expansion prices)
nba.franchise_valuation_comps.mechanism: A headline franchise value is drawn from the distribution of recent sale and expansion prices, scaled by market size and revenue growth, so P(value above strike) comes from a predictive distribution over comparables, not a base rate of events.
nba.franchise_valuation_comps.rationale: KXNBAFRANCHISECOST resolves on a headline enterprise value above a strike after bundled assets are stripped; the event base rate says only whether a sale happens, whereas the strike probability needs a valuation model built from comparable transactions and the league's expansion-fee reporting.
nba.franchise_valuation_comps.measurement: Collect headline enterprise values of NBA franchise sales and expansion fees 2015-2026 with market, year and reported separable asset adjustments; regress log(value) on the prior-year published franchise valuation, revenue growth and market size; predictive sd from residuals (inflate for expansion franchises, which have no comparables); P(headline > strike) from the predictive distribution, then multiply by P(qualifying sale announced and approved within the window) from the approval pipeline.
raw_data: franchise sale and expansion-fee headline values with dates
nba.franchise_valuation_comps.why: Gives the strike probability for franchise-cost markets a market-free valuation model.

nba.next_contract_value_model.label: Next-contract value distribution (maximum and minimum tiers, Bird rights, comparables)
nba.next_contract_value_model.mechanism: A player's next contract is bounded by the CBA's maximum tiers (a percentage of the cap by years of service) and minimums, and within that range set by comparable deals, his impact and age, and the cap space of teams that want him, with Bird rights letting the incumbent team exceed the cap.
nba.next_contract_value_model.rationale: KXNBANEXTCONTRACT is a contract-size market kept under this key by the reconciliation, and no other input here produces a value distribution. Many star contracts sit exactly at the maximum, so the distribution has a point mass at the tier cap (a strike just below the max is near certain for a max-level player); the projected cap for the signing season moves the dollar value of the max, and extensions versus free agency have different ceilings.
nba.next_contract_value_model.measurement: For the named player compute his maximum tier from years of service (recalled 25/30/35% of the cap and the designated-veteran criteria, to be checked) and the projected cap for the signing season from the league's published projection; model value as a share of the cap with a censored (Tobit) regression at the max and the minimum on age, prior two-season impact (box plus-minus type metric), minutes, All-NBA status and position, fitted on the last 6 free-agency and extension classes; years and annual value modelled jointly; simulate destination with nba.player_move_destination_model to apply cap-space feasibility. As-of: the market timestamp, updated on reported negotiations.
free_sources: Spotrac contract and cap database (free pages)
raw_data: signed contracts by player (years, total value, AAV, signing type) for 6 seasons
player impact and minutes by season
nba.next_contract_value_model.why: KXNBANEXTCONTRACT settles on the size of the player's next contract, which requires a value distribution with a point mass at the maximum tier.

nba.news.reason: An undifferentiated news feed; without stage and source reliability it cannot be turned into a probability, which the reporter reliability score supplies.

nba.transaction_flow.reason: Rule-feasibility (cap, apron, roster, moratorium) is the cleanest gate for trades and signings; needs a concrete salary-matching checker and a payroll snapshot.

nba.org_stability.reason: Coach and front-office hazard based on record versus expectation is reasonable but needs the preseason expectation measure and a historical reference class.

nba.all_star_process.reason: Relevant to the All-Star participant item in the label, but no live series here depends on it; it overlaps the awards archetype's All-Star starters series.

nba.calendar_announcements.reason: Official schedule and deadline dates are known inputs to the hazard; the entry lacks an hazard profile and Eastern Time boundary handling.

nba.standings_motivation.reason: Competitive pressure explains coach and trade timing only loosely; most live markets here are ownership or league events where standings are irrelevant.

nba.injury_risk_season.reason: Season-level availability risk has little bearing on franchise sales or rule changes; relevant only to a few player-decision markets, where career horizon is more apt.

nba.draft_board.reason: Draft order informs pick trades only; none of the sampled series (sales, governor, retirement, rule adoption, expansion) depend on it.

nba.offfield_base_rate.reason: Reference-class frequencies are the right prior for sale, relocation and rule-change markets, but pooled base rates need conditioning on the specific window and stage.

m.quote_history.reason: Illiquid event markets move on reports; the price path helps date information arrival but is not a driver of whether the event occurs.

m.rules_text.reason: Versioned rules text defines the settled quantity for the off-court event markets; wording changes between series are the only way to know the target variable, so it is a required contract input, not a feature.

m.lifecycle.reason: Market open/close/expiration timing for the off-court event markets defines the information horizon at which any estimate must be as-of; context only.

interactions.mechanism: A top-tier report that an agreement is signed multiplies with the remaining approval pipeline probability; a reliable report at the agreed stage still leaves the approval and timing risk, so the market should not jump to one.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare outcomes of deals reported at 'agreed' by reliable sources against the share that cleared approval within 90 days.

interactions.mechanism: Trade probability collapses after the deadline and spikes in the days before it, so the hazard is convex in days to deadline; feasibility constraints bind most tightly in the last week when salary-matching is tested.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the daily hazard around the deadline with and without a feasibility flag; test hazard ratio at days -3 to 0.

interactions.mechanism: Coach-firing hazard is near zero above expectation but rises sharply once a team falls below a record-versus-expectation threshold or loses a streak; the combination of underperformance and ownership impatience acts as a trigger.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate a hazard model with a hinge at the expectation gap and test slope change.

interactions.mechanism: The same news item resolves differently under different wordings: an agreement in principle satisfies an announcement market but not a definitive-agreement or approved-sale market, so one report moves the series in opposite directions.
interactions.how_to_test: Code each historical report against each wording in the series set and measure the divergence in outcomes.

interactions.mechanism: A retirement announcement clusters after the season ends and before free agency, so the player's age hazard is conditional on being in that period; before the season's end the hazard is lower regardless of age.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate retirement announcement timing by month for players aged 36+ and test the seasonal hazard ratio.

nonlinearities.shape: Spiked and convex around deadlines
nonlinearities.why: The probability mass of trades concentrates in the final days before a deadline and then goes to zero, so linear time decay misprices markets near the deadline.

nonlinearities.shape: Step function by stage
nonlinearities.why: Probability to complete jumps at each stage (exploration about 0.2, definitive agreement about 0.9) rather than rising smoothly with time, and timing risk is lognormal.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating in report stage
nonlinearities.why: Reports at the agreed stage from tier-one sources approach 1, while talks-stage reports sit near 0.1-0.3, so credence is not linear in the intensity of the language.

nonlinearities.shape: Logistic threshold in the record-vs-expectation gap
nonlinearities.why: Firing hazard is near flat for modest underperformance and rises quickly after a threshold, typically in the first third of the season or after a long losing streak.

required_data.dataset: Rules text and close times for every live off-court series
required_data.timestamp_requirement: Versioned at market issuance; store hash and snapshot.
Time stamp of first credible report and official act.
As-of date; payroll snapshots after each transaction.
Date each stage was reached.
As-of date; statements dated.

required_data.dataset: Rule proposals, Board of Governors votes and franchise price comparables
required_data.timestamp_requirement: Date of each stage or announcement; use only items announced before the as-of time.
required_data.history_needed: 2000-2026 for rule proposals; 2015-2026 for franchise prices

candidate_sources.name: NBA.com official announcements and Board of Governors releases

required_data.grain: one row per signed contract; one row per season for cap projections
required_data.timestamp_requirement: contracts by signing date and cap projections by publication date, so a backtest uses only what was public at the market timestamp

candidate_sources.name: Spotrac
candidate_sources.note: contract details; some fields behind a paid tier

candidate_sources.name: League cap projection memos via reporters
candidate_sources.note: projections are reported, not published as a dataset

unresolved.what_would_resolve: Sample rules_primary and rules_secondary for each remaining series and code the qualifying stage.

unresolved.description: Private negotiations, the content of owner meetings and the number of active bidders are unobservable; probabilities of sales and expansion rely on leaks and reference classes with few observations per event type.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: No public source; accept wide uncertainty or use reporter-reliability proxies; consider paid deal-intelligence services.

unresolved.description: The league's approval threshold for franchise sales (a supermajority of owners) and the typical durations between definitive agreement and approval are recalled from general knowledge and not verified from the current league constitution or recent deals.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Read the league constitution or credible coverage of recent approvals and tabulate dates.

A rule-adoption pipeline and a valuation reference class are now defined (nba.rule_change_pipeline, nba.franchise_valuation_comps), but the stadium-completion project timeline is still unmeasured.

Per-type inputs now exist only for rule changes and franchise values; sales, relocation and the remaining families still share the pooled base rate.
