contract.settlement_definition: After the reconciliation both live escalator series are filed under this key, KXNBAESCALATORPTS and KXNBAESCALATOR3PT, each with sampled rules text. Both are scalar markets whose Yes payout is a cubic function of a single-game count: points use floor(10000 x (y / 50)^3) / 10000 with y = min(50, max(0, 2 x floor(s / 2))) and threes use floor(10000 x (y / 10)^3) / 10000 with y = min(10, s); No pays 1 minus the Yes payout and a zero count pays Yes $0.00. The economic quantity is therefore E[g(K)] with g cubic and capped at 50 points or 10 threes, not a threshold probability. The treatment of a player who is inactive, never takes the court or exits early is not visible in the sampled text (the points rules_primary is truncated at 600 characters) and is CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS; a zero count paying Yes $0.00 suggests a non-appearance pays the lowest band, but that is an inference.

rules_evidence.quote: Payout Formula = floor(10000 x (y / 50)^3) / 10000 y = min(50, max(0, 2 x floor(s / 2))) s = official player points
rules_evidence.establishes: Points escalator pays a cubic function of points rounded down to an even number and capped at 50, so 24 and 25 points pay the same and 50+ pays $1.00; the value is E[g(K)], not a threshold probability.

rules_evidence.quote: Payout Formula = floor(10000 x (y / 10)^3) / 10000 y = min(10, s) s = official player made three-pointers
rules_evidence.establishes: Threes escalator pays (threes/10)^3 floored to 1/10000, capped at 10 made threes, so 5 threes pay $0.125 and 7 pay $0.343.

rules_evidence.quote: Zero made three-pointers recorded pays Yes $0.00.
rules_evidence.establishes: A zero count pays nothing; the text says nothing about an inactive or never-on-court player, so the non-appearance treatment is unseen (u1).

variants_and_edge_cases: Two live variants with different resolution: points settle on 2-point bands (y = 2 x floor(s/2), so 24 and 25 points pay the same, 50 or more points pay $1.00) and threes settle on single made threes with a payout of $1.00 at 10 or more.

Cubic payout: g = (y/cap)^3 puts most of the expected value in the upper tail (a 5-three game pays $0.125, a 7-three game $0.343), so the contract is far more sensitive to tail probability than to the mean.
Cap: the formulas cap y at 50 points and 10 threes, so extreme tails beyond the cap carry no extra payout and only P(K >= cap) matters there.

Non-appearance: the sampled text does not say how an inactive or never-on-court player is paid (a fair-price void as in the threshold ladders, or a zero count paying the lowest band, an opposite treatment); the points rules_primary is truncated at 600 characters.
Parity: 2-point points bands mean an odd free throw moves mass between adjacent bands only through the floor, so free-throw and three-point parity shifts the pmf over bands.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official box score points or made threes for the named player and game; the payout table and formula come from the contract text.

mechanism.summary: A scalar-payout contract pays a function g(K) of a single-game count K, so its value is the expectation of g over the whole distribution of K, and a convex g puts most of the expected value in the upper tail where data are scarce. The distribution is built from stages: whether and how long the player plays (a mixture of normal, truncated, extended and overtime games), how many attempts occur (for threes, attempts depend on role and spacing; for points, on usage and free-throw trips), and what fraction convert (a binomial with extra within-game dispersion because shooting is clustered, not independent). Then points are a composite 2 x FG2 + 3 x FG3 + FT, so a 2-point band is a statement about the sum with parity effects from free throws. The tail beyond the 90th percentile is generated by rare combinations: high minutes plus high attempts plus hot shooting, so the payout depends on the joint upper tail rather than on any single factor, and on shrinkage choices for make rates which change the tail non-linearly.

stages.name: Payout schedule operator
stages.description: The contract defines g(K) in its rules text: band edges, payout per band, a top band that may be open-ended, rounding and the treatment of non-appearance. The value of the contract is sum over K of P(K) g(K), so the schedule is a part of the model: a convex schedule up-weights the 95th-99th percentile outcomes, a capped schedule cuts the extreme tail and a floor schedule pays something for low counts. The two live schedules are cubic and capped: points pay (y/50)^3 with y = min(50, 2 x floor(s/2)), threes pay (min(10,s)/10)^3.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the text; the information content is in how g weights the pmf (convexity, cap, void rule).

stages.name: Playing time and extreme-minutes tail
stages.description: Minutes set the number of attempts, and the right tail of minutes (38 to 44 minutes in close games or overtime) generates the largest counts. The probability of heavy minutes depends on closeness of the expected game, bench quality, foul trouble and the coach's habit with stars; overtime adds five minutes with a probability near six percent. A truncated blowout night produces the low band and can be bounded by the payout floor.
stages.distribution: Right-tailed mixture with a heavy-minute component of 10-20% for stars and a point mass near the low band for blowouts.

stages.name: Attempt volume
stages.description: Attempts are the count of opportunities: three-point attempts depend on role (catch-and-shoot share), opponent concession of threes and team pace; field-goal attempts for the points escalator depend on usage and free-throw trips. Attempt counts are overdispersed with game-to-game sd roughly 30-40% of the mean, and they covary with minutes and with team scoring environment.
stages.distribution: Negative-binomial-like counts; attempts per minute vary by game script and by opposing scheme; correlation with minutes about 0.6-0.7.

stages.name: Make rate with within-game clustering
stages.description: Make probability per attempt is a skill parameter shrunk toward the player's long-run rate, but within a game makes cluster beyond a binomial because of shot quality sequences and defensive attention, so the count of makes is a beta-binomial with an intra-game correlation of about 0.02-0.05. Overdispersion widens both tails and increases the weight of high counts that a convex schedule rewards; shrinkage of the rate to the mean lowers the tail.
stages.distribution: Beta-binomial with rho about 0.03: variance increases about 15-30% beyond binomial for 10-attempt games (approximate, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED).

stages.name: Composite points parity and the joint tail
stages.description: For the points schedule the count is 2 FG2 + 3 FG3 + FTM, a composite whose parity and band mass depend on free throws and threes; the pmf over 2-point bands is not the same as that over single points. The expected payout is the sum over the composite pmf, and the upper tail needs the joint of minutes, attempts, make rate and free-throw trips, which is a copula problem rather than a product of marginals.
stages.distribution: Composite integer distribution with parity structure; upper tail from the joint of volume and luck.

talent_strength.note: Shooting skill (shrunk) and team strength as it affects the script.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent concession of three-point attempts and defence profile.

role_personnel.note: Role determines volume and the chance of heavy minutes.

availability_news.note: Own and teammate status; also drives void rules.

coaching_scheme.note: Scheme influences attempt allocation, but the information is in usage and three-point volume; a distinct coaching input would duplicate those and no specific scheme variable for scalar payouts is warranted.

environment.note: Altitude and venue have no credible direct effect on a single player's count beyond pace and rest, which are already in the volume and minutes drivers.

game_context_script.note: Blowouts and closeness set the minutes mixture.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, back-to-back and late-season incentives alter the chance of heavy minutes for stars, but no input in this archetype quantifies the schedule-driven change in the heavy-minutes tail.

officiating_rules.note: Crew effects change free-throw counts, a minor part of the points composite, and no evidence links crew identity to the three-point count; the ft_attempts input captures the foul-driven component.

settlement_contract.note: Payout formulas are known for the points and threes escalators from sampled rules_secondary (cubic, capped at 50 points and 10 threes, zero count pays $0.00); the non-appearance rule and protected variants remain unseen (u1).

nba.payout_schedule_operator.label: Payout schedule operator g(K) parsed from rules text
nba.payout_schedule_operator.mechanism: The contract's value is E[g(K)] where g is the payout table in the rules text, so the schedule is part of the model.
nba.payout_schedule_operator.rationale: The cubic schedule means value is dominated by the upper tail: for threes with mean 3 the payout at the mean is $0.027, but the expected payout is much higher because 5+ made threes pay $0.125 or more. The operator must therefore be part of the model, not a post-hoc transform.
nba.payout_schedule_operator.measurement: Implement the two live schedules exactly: points g(s) = floor(10000 x (y/50)^3)/10000 with y = min(50, max(0, 2 x floor(s/2))); threes g(s) = floor(10000 x (y/10)^3)/10000 with y = min(10, s); parse any new schedule from rules_primary/rules_secondary into (band_lo, band_hi, payout) arrays and cap/void fields and check monotonicity against the formula; value = sum over k of P(K=k) g(k); compute sensitivity of value to mean, variance and P(K >= cap) by finite differences; version the parser by rules hash and flag unparsed tables.
nba.payout_schedule_operator.why: A convex schedule shifts value into the upper tail, and the exact shape of g decides which probabilities matter.

nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.label: Probability of heavy-minutes games (38+ minutes, OT)
nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.mechanism: The extreme counts come from nights with heavy minutes, whose probability depends on game closeness, depth and the coach's usage of the star.
nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.rationale: A single projected minutes figure hides the 10-20% of nights with 38+ minutes that produce the top bands, and nights with 20-25 minutes that produce the bottom ones.
nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.measurement: Per player: share of games with minutes >= 38 over the last 80 games (half-life 30), shrunk to role prior with k=15 games; condition on own-model closeness (P(|margin| < 8) from the margin model) and OT probability 0.06; produce P(minutes >= 38) and mean count in that regime = rate per minute x 40; as-of lineup status.
nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.why: The convex payout puts weight on heavy-minute games, so the probability of that regime is a primary driver.

nba.within_game_make_dispersion.label: Within-game make-rate dispersion (beta-binomial rho)
nba.within_game_make_dispersion.mechanism: Makes in a game are positively correlated beyond independent shots, so the count is overdispersed relative to a binomial.
nba.within_game_make_dispersion.rationale: Independence understates the tail of makes, which a convex payout over-weights; the dispersion parameter is a key tail parameter.
nba.within_game_make_dispersion.measurement: Estimate rho by maximum likelihood of a beta-binomial model on 5 seasons of player-game (attempts, makes) for players with at least 200 attempts; pool by shot type (three, two, free throw) and by attempt count; shrink the player-specific rho to the pooled value with k=100 games; produce the pmf of makes given attempts n and rate p.
raw_data: player-game attempts and makes by type
nba.within_game_make_dispersion.why: Directly sets the upper-tail probability for 5+ threes or 35+ points under a convex payout.

nba.points_parity_band_mass.label: Composite points pmf with parity and free-throw effect for 2-point bands
nba.points_parity_band_mass.mechanism: Points = 2 FG2 + 3 FG3 + FT; the mass of a 2-point band depends on parity coming from threes and free throws.
nba.points_parity_band_mass.rationale: Band probabilities from a smooth normal approximation ignore the lattice structure of the composite, which can misallocate up to several percentage points between adjacent bands.
nba.points_parity_band_mass.measurement: Simulate FG2, FG3, FT counts with beta-binomial dispersion and component correlations estimated on 5 seasons; tabulate P(points = k) and aggregate to band edges from the rules; verify pmf mod 2 against historical frequencies; shrink the pmf to the smoothed empirical pmf of similar-usage players with weight 0.2.
nba.points_parity_band_mass.why: A points escalator in 2-point bands is a lattice problem; parity affects band masses.

nba.early_exit_hazard.label: Protected-void probability: first-half-only participation (injury, ejection, illness or coach-rested second half)
nba.early_exit_hazard.mechanism: P(player enters in the first half but never after halftime, including OT) = injury/ejection/illness exit hazard plus the coach decision to rest him for the whole second half in a lopsided game; the protected clause voids both unless the strike was already reached.
nba.early_exit_hazard.rationale: Early exit by injury is only one route to the void state: the sampled protected text voids any player who enters in the first half and does not enter after it, so a starter pulled for the entire second half of a first-half blowout is also void. Both routes are unrelated to per-minute rates and the second is strongly tied to the first-half margin.
nba.early_exit_hazard.measurement: Two components over the last 3 seasons. (a) Injury/ejection/illness exit hazard h = exits (left and did not return) / minutes, shrunk to a position prior with k=2000 minutes and scaled by 1.5 for the first 3 games after a listed injury; P(exit before half) = 1 - exp(-h*minutes_in_half1). (b) Coach-rest route: from play-by-play, P(no second-half entry | played first half and non-injury) by own-model pregame spread bucket and coach, estimated on 3 seasons with beta shrinkage k=30 games; combine as 1-(1-a)(1-b); then convert by contract wording (protected void vs actual stats, with the strike-already-reached carve-out).
nba.early_exit_hazard.why: The escalator pays on the realised count, so an in-game exit truncates minutes and the lower bands, and the non-appearance branch may void or pay zero depending on the unseen rule; the hazard gives P(zero or truncated minutes) separately from injury status.

nba.teammate_absence_shift.label: With/without teammate splits: usage, minutes and stat redistribution
nba.teammate_absence_shift.mechanism: When key teammates are out, shot attempts, ball-handling, and rebound opportunities redistribute to the remaining players in a structured way (not evenly).
nba.teammate_absence_shift.rationale: This is the largest edge source for props: a lead guard out raises the backup guard's usage and assists, but a primary scorer out lowers assists for his passing partner (fewer converted passes). Direction depends on whether the absent player consumes the stat (usage, rebounds) or produces teammates' stat conversion (shooters). Subtle: with/without samples are small and confounded by opponent and by injuries to multiple players; use hierarchical shrinkage and role-based priors.
nba.teammate_absence_shift.measurement: Per player: stat per minute and minutes with teammate X on/off the roster, over games where X missed; hierarchical shrinkage to a role-based redistribution model (usage, ball handling, rebound share absorbed); evaluate for combinations of absences.
free_sources: PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)
nba.teammate_absence_shift.why: A missing creator or scorer raises a player's attempts and heavy-minutes probability, shifting the whole tail of a cubic payout.

nba.fga_per_minute_by_shot_type.label: Field-goal attempts per minute split into two-point and three-point attempts, with free-throw trip rate
nba.fga_per_minute_by_shot_type.mechanism: Points = 2 x made 2PT + 3 x made 3PT + FTM, so each component needs its own attempt rate per minute rather than a blended usage rate that includes turnovers.
nba.fga_per_minute_by_shot_type.rationale: The points escalator needs FGA per minute by type and free-throw trips per minute as the volume base for the cubic payout; usage rate mixes in turnovers and free-throw trips, and the audit of nba.usage asks for this replacement.
nba.fga_per_minute_by_shot_type.measurement: 2PA, 3PA and FTA per 36 minutes over the last 2 seasons with weights 0.6 recent / 0.4 prior and half-life 20 games, shrunk to the role-position mean with k=300 minutes; scale by the projected minutes scenario mixture and add the with/without-teammate shift from the teammate-absence splits; output a per-minute rate and its sd for use in a negative-binomial attempt model.
nba.fga_per_minute_by_shot_type.why: Escalator points need a clean attempt volume by shot type; usage is an imperfect proxy.

nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.label: Ratings-based blowout probability and starter-minutes-vs-margin curve (market-free)
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.mechanism: Rebuilds the blowout risk from team strength and rotation history instead of the closing spread: a ratings-implied expected margin and margin spread give P(large lead), and a coach/player minutes-versus-margin curve converts each margin path into expected minutes lost by starters and gained by bench players.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.rationale: The catalog input nba.garbage is defined from the closing spread, which is a market price and so a benchmark, not an input. The causal quantity is the chance that the margin passes the coach's pull threshold early enough to matter, and how much playing time each player then loses. Subtle: the loss depends on when the lead arrives (a 20-point lead entering Q4 removes far more starter minutes than one reached with 3 minutes left), on the coach, and on whether the trailing team also pulls starters, so the curve must be conditional on the margin path and not only on the final margin.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.measurement: Step 1, expected margin: mu = (NetRtg_home_adj - NetRtg_away_adj) * expected_possessions/100 + home_adv, where NetRtg_adj is the as-of-tipoff opponent-adjusted net rating from nba.off_rtg and nba.def_rtg (ridge regression on game point differential, half-life about 25 games, shrunk to the preseason prior with n_prior about 20 games as a placeholder to be fitted), adjusted for the confirmed unavailable players via nba.lineup_adj_rating, home_adv fitted on the last 5 seasons (about 2 points). Step 2, margin spread: sd_margin fitted on 5 seasons of residuals of final margin versus mu (league-wide roughly 12-13 points, to be estimated, with a heavier empirical tail than normal). Step 3: P(final |margin| >= 15/20/25) and P(|lead| >= 15/20 entering Q4) from the empirical residual distribution around mu. Step 4, minutes curve: from play-by-play stints, per team-season, expected minutes of each rotation player conditional on margin entering Q4 in bins (0-9, 10-14, 15-19, 20+), shrunk toward the league curve with k about 30 blowout games. Output per player: expected minutes lost and the probability of falling below a stated minutes level. No closing line or other price is used; the spread is retained only to benchmark calibration of step 3.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com leaguegamelog (team game logs, free, undocumented, rate-limited)
cdn.nba.com liveData playbyplay JSON (substitutions with score, free, unofficial)
Basketball-Reference game logs and play-by-play (free, polite scraping)
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.why: Replaces the spread-based nba.garbage in player_escalator_payout: blowout truncation of the relevant players' minutes from own ratings and the coach's pull curve, with no closing line used.
raw_data: team-game final margins and opponent-adjusted ratings as of tipoff (5 seasons)
play-by-play substitution stints with margin entering Q4 (per team-season)

nba.stat_dist.reason: The full count distribution is the object here, but it must be a composite built from minutes, attempts and make dispersion, not a fitted marginal to the stat alone.

nba.minutes.reason: Scenario mixture of minutes drives the tail, but the entry describes a projection; the heavy-minute probability must be explicit.

nba.three_volume.reason: Attempt rate and catch-and-shoot share is the main driver for the threes escalator; the shrinkage of 3P% is separately needed.

nba.usage.reason: Shot share drives the points escalator; usage lumps free-throw trips and turnovers so FGA per minute is the cleaner variable.

nba.player_shooting_regression.reason: Shrinking make rates is correct, but its choice of shrinkage controls the tail non-linearly, so it should be reported as a sensitivity rather than a single value.

nba.garbage.reason: Catalog definition is 'Blowout / garbage-time probability from spread' (measurement: P(final |margin| > 15/20/25) as a function of the closing spread), so as defined it is market-derived and only a calibration benchmark; the blowout-minutes mechanism is carried by the market-free nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve (ratings-implied margin plus coach minutes-versus-margin curve).

nba.ft_attempts.reason: Free-throw points are part of the points composite and add parity, but irrelevant for the threes escalator.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Status vintages determine participation and the payout rule for non-appearance; teammates' status shifts volume.

nba.pace.reason: Possessions scale attempts modestly; effect on tail is dominated by minutes and role.

nba.ratings.reason: Team season ratings are a coarse proxy for blowout risk already captured by the margin model; the rationale conflates team strength with individual usage.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price path for the scalar-payout contract; useful to see when information was absorbed and for calibration labels, but it is an observation of the market, never an explanatory driver of the outcome.

m.rules_text.reason: Versioned rules text defines the settled quantity for the scalar-payout contract; wording changes between series are the only way to know the target variable, so it is a required contract input, not a feature.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Cross-rung consistency applies to threshold ladders; for a scalar payout there is a single price and the implied distribution is not observable from it.

interactions.mechanism: The top bands are reached when a heavy-minutes game coincides with hot shooting, and since both are rare, their joint probability determines the tail; the product of marginal tail probabilities underestimates it when close games also increase attempts.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate joint tail frequencies of (minutes >= 38, makes in top decile) and compare to the product.

interactions.mechanism: The count of made threes is attempts times make rate, so the tail is convex in both; over-shrinking the make rate shrinks the tail multiplicatively while a high-attempt shooter's tail is more sensitive to the rate.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute tail probability sensitivity to shrinkage constant k for low versus high attempt shooters.

interactions.mechanism: Under a convex payout, expected value is more than the payout at the mean (Jensen), so overdispersion raises value and an underestimate of variance understates it; the effect is larger the steeper the schedule.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute E[g(K)] with the fitted pmf and with the same mean but lower variance, report the difference.

interactions.mechanism: In a blowout the starter's minutes drop and the count falls to low bands; since the payout is convex, losing the upper tail costs more than the shift of the mean, and the effect appears beyond a expected margin threshold of about 10 points.
interactions.how_to_test: Stratify games by expected margin and compute realised mean payout versus the prediction using the mean only.

interactions.mechanism: Free-throw trips add odd points that move outcomes between 2-point bands; for a player with high FTA the parity of the composite matters more than for a pure jump shooter, so the band mass is conditional on FT mix.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare predicted band masses with and without parity modelling for high-FTA players.

nonlinearities.shape: Cubic payoff capped at 50 points or 10 threes
nonlinearities.why: A cubic schedule gives disproportionate weight to the right tail (a 7-three game pays $0.343 versus $0.027 for 3), so a small change in tail probability moves expected payout far more than a change in the mean, and the cap removes value beyond 50 points or 10 threes.

nonlinearities.shape: Overdispersion widens both tails
nonlinearities.why: Beta-binomial clustering raises the probability of 5+ makes beyond a binomial, an effect that grows with attempts.

nonlinearities.shape: Mixture with a heavy-minutes bump
nonlinearities.why: Counts in a 40-minute game are not a stretched version of a 32-minute game but a separate regime with higher attempts and fatigue effects, so the response to minutes is piecewise.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave shrinkage in the sample size
nonlinearities.why: Weight on a player's recent make rate grows slowly with attempts (about 0.3 at 100 attempts), so the tail is sensitive to small-sample extremes.

contract.settlement_definition: No live series is filed under this archetype key and no rules text exists, so the contract is NOT_VERIFIED. By analogy with the NBA player-stat ladders that are live (assists, combos), a free-throws-made contract would settle Yes if the named player makes at least N free throws in the named game, with a half-point strike, a fair-price void for a player who is inactive or never takes the court, possible protected variants for first-half-only appearances, overtime free throws counted through the official box score, and a short postponement staying open. These analogies are inferences and none of them is verified for free throws; technical and flagrant free throws, and whether free throws in overtime count, are specific unknowns. Every input role in this record is therefore conditional on a free-throws-made contract being listed (see u5).
variants_and_edge_cases: Technical, flagrant and clear-path free throws are made by the player (or a designated shooter) and count in the box score as free throws made, but whether the contract counts them is unseen.
Overtime free throws, which concentrate in intentional-foul situations in close games, add attempts; inclusion is likely but not stated.
Void and protected variants: an inactive player or a first-half-only appearance may void at fair price, as in other player-stat series, but this is not verified.
Strike construction: 'N+' integers with a half-point floor strike would be survival probabilities of a binomial-mixture count with a mass at zero for low-volume players.
A player who makes zero attempts is a valid outcome (not void) once he plays, which creates a large mass at zero for non-shooters.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official box score free-throws-made count, with later stat corrections; the substitution/play-by-play record for any protected clause.

mechanism.summary: Free throws made = free throw attempts x make probability, and the two factors have very different properties. Attempts are an event count generated by foul-drawing: trips to the line come from shooting fouls on drives and post-ups, non-shooting fouls once the opponent is in the bonus (five team fouls in the period), technicals, and intentional fouls late in close games. Each trip yields one to three attempts, so attempts are clustered, not independent. The make probability is a stable skill, around 0.75-0.85 for guards and 0.55-0.70 for many bigs, and conditional on attempts the number of makes is nearly binomial. So variance comes mostly from attempts, which depend on minutes, the player's drive and post frequency, the opponent's foul rate, the crew's whistle, the game's closeness (late-game fouling targets poor shooters and rewards the trailing team's fouls on stars), and on the bonus state. The count has a heavy right tail from close games with intentional fouls and is zero for many games for low-volume players.

stages.name: Floor time and role in the offence
stages.description: Free throws are drawn while on court and mostly while attacking the rim or posting up, so minutes and the number of such actions set exposure. A guard who attacks the rim 8 times per game and a spot-up wing with 2 rim attempts have attempt means of about 6 versus 1.5. Blowouts remove the late free-throw-rich minutes, while close games add them for the leading team's ball handlers.
stages.distribution: Mixture over minutes regimes; attempts per minute vary by role by a factor of five or more; count of trips overdispersed.

stages.name: Trip generation: shooting fouls and bonus state
stages.description: Trips arise from shooting fouls (rate per drive or rim attempt), non-shooting fouls in the bonus, offensive fouls that do not give shots, and technical or flagrant calls. The opponent's foul-committing rate, its defensive style (rim protection without fouling vs aggressive), the crew and the team-foul state of the period determine how many of the player's actions end at the line. The trip count is clustered and has a handful of possible attempt sizes (1, 2, 3).
stages.distribution: Poisson-like trip count with overdispersion; attempts per trip 2 with probabilities of 3 and 1; bonus state creates time-varying hazard within each quarter.

stages.name: Late-game fouling and intentional-foul targets
stages.description: In the last two minutes of close games the trailing team fouls to stop the clock, choosing who is fouled: poor free-throw shooters are targeted when the rule allows, and the leading team's ball handlers collect many attempts. The probability that a given player is a target depends on his free-throw percentage, his role as a ball handler and the margin and time left. This creates a right tail concentrated in close games and a hack-a-big regime for low-percentage shooters. Mid-game hack-a-player fouling away from the ball in Q1-Q3 is a separate, rarer route that depends on the opposing coach and the target's free-throw percentage and is carried as an extra bonus-state term.
stages.distribution: Conditional tail: in games within 6 points with two minutes left, attempts jump by 3-6 for ball handlers; the target rate depends on a threshold in FT% below about 60%.

stages.name: Per-attempt conversion skill
stages.description: Each attempt converts with the player's free-throw skill, which has a high signal-to-noise ratio: 200 attempts pin a rate to about 3 percentage points, and rates are persistent across seasons. For young or low-volume players the career-based estimate is noisy and informative priors come from other shooting (three-point, mid-range) and pre-NBA free-throw records. Within-game, makes are close to independent, so conditional on attempts the count is binomial.
stages.distribution: Binomial given attempts with p known to within about 3-5 points; variance largest at p near 0.5.

stages.name: Count distribution and threshold
stages.description: Making N free throws requires at least N attempts, so P(FTM >= N) = sum over attempts a >= N of P(attempts = a) times Binomial tail; the zero mass for low-volume players and the heavy right tail for stars at the line make the distribution far from normal. Settlement via the official box score is unlikely to be corrected often, but the half-point strike at integer counts means adjacent rungs differ by P(FTM = k).
stages.distribution: Mixture of a negative-binomial attempt distribution with a binomial thinning; mean 4-7 and sd 3-4 for high-volume players; zero-inflated for low-volume.

nba.ft_trip_structure_model.label: Free-throw trip generation model (trips x attempts per trip)
nba.ft_trip_structure_model.mechanism: Attempts are the sum of trips (shooting fouls, bonus fouls, technicals, intentional fouls) times attempts per trip (1, 2, 3).
nba.ft_trip_structure_model.rationale: The draft's ft_attempts is a rate; the clustered structure of trips matters for the variance and for the survival function at N.
nba.ft_trip_structure_model.measurement: Per player: trips per 36 = shooting-foul trips (per 100 rim attempts and per 100 post touches) + bonus trips (per team-bonus minute) + other; attempts per trip distribution from his shot mix (share of 3PA fouled, and-one rate); estimate with 3 seasons of play-by-play, shrinkage k=60 trips to position prior; simulate trips with negative-binomial dispersion estimated across games.
nba.ft_trip_structure_model.why: A trip-based model gives both mean and clustering, which settle N+ strike rungs.

nba.bonus_state_foul_environment.label: Bonus-state and team-foul environment
nba.bonus_state_foul_environment.mechanism: Non-shooting fouls turn into free throws once the defending team is in the bonus, so the opponent's team foul rate and bonus minutes drive attempts.
nba.bonus_state_foul_environment.rationale: Opponent foul rate enters twice (shooting fouls and bonus fouls), and the draft's foul rate input does not separate the bonus effect.
nba.bonus_state_foul_environment.measurement: Opponent team personal fouls per quarter, share of quarter minutes in bonus (from play-by-play), crew fouls per game; combine as bonus_minutes_expected = f(opponent foul rate, crew rate, own pace) using 3 seasons; each bonus minute adds a rate of player-specific non-shooting-foul attempts (estimated from the player's FTA in bonus vs non-bonus minutes with shrinkage k=40 minutes).
raw_data: foul events with team foul count, quarter, crew
nba.bonus_state_foul_environment.why: Bonus time is a mechanical pathway that scales every ball handler's attempts.

nba.intentional_foul_target_prob.label: Intentional-foul target probability (hack-a policy and late-game ball handlers)
nba.intentional_foul_target_prob.mechanism: Probability that the player is fouled intentionally in the last two minutes of a close game, as a function of FT%, role and margin. Mid-game hack-a-player fouling in Q1-Q3 is included as a separate, rarer component.
nba.intentional_foul_target_prob.rationale: Late-game attempts form the right tail; whether a player is a target depends on a threshold in FT% for bigs and on being the leading team's ball handler.
nba.intentional_foul_target_prob.measurement: Per player: attempts in the last 2 minutes of games within 6 points per 100 such minutes (last 3 seasons, shrinkage k=30 minutes); logistic target model with features FT% (below 0.60 flag), ball-handler role, trailing/leading, margin; combine with own-model P(close at 2:00) to give expected additional attempts; update each season after rule changes. Add an early-game component: frequency of intentional away-from-the-ball or hack-a fouls in Q1-Q3 per 100 possessions by opposing coach and target (from play-by-play foul descriptions); outside the last two minutes these are ordinary personal fouls that yield free throws only through the bonus, so they are modelled as extra bonus-state attempts for the targeted low-FT% player.
raw_data: late-game foul events with margin and clock
nba.intentional_foul_target_prob.why: The right tail of free throws comes from these games and is concentrated among a few players.

nba.ft_skill_posterior.label: Free-throw skill posterior (career, three-point, pre-NBA priors)
nba.ft_skill_posterior.mechanism: Make probability is a skill with informative priors for low-sample players.
nba.ft_skill_posterior.rationale: Free-throw percentage over a short sample is noisy; for rookies and low-volume players, three-point percentage and pre-NBA free-throw data improve the estimate.
nba.ft_skill_posterior.measurement: p_hat = (FTM_3y_weighted + a) / (FTA_3y_weighted + a + b), with weights 0.5/0.3/0.2 by season, prior (a, b) from a regression of FT% on 3P% (slope about 0.5 at 100 3PA, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED) and pre-NBA FT% for rookies, effective prior size 80 attempts; report sd of posterior.
raw_data: career FT and 3P attempts and makes
nba.ft_skill_posterior.why: Distinguishes a 60% center from a 75% guard and gives uncertainty for new players.

nba.injuries_pit.label: Injury report (official + ESPN) vintages, status changes
nba.injuries_pit.mechanism: Player status (out, doubtful, questionable, probable) as of a timestamp determines who plays, and hence minutes, usage and team strength.
nba.injuries_pit.rationale: The official report is posted in waves (afternoon the day before, updates through game day) and final inactives appear ~30-90 minutes before tip, so at a given decision time status is often only partially resolved. Status labels are not calibrated probabilities: 'questionable' resolves differently by team, player age, injury type and back-to-back. Subtle: the report vintage (not the final inactive list) is the legitimate pregame feature.
nba.injuries_pit.measurement: Archive every report snapshot with retrieved_at; per player: status, reason text, time of last change, number of status flips; feature as-of decision time; link to final actual availability only as a label.
free_sources: NBA official injury report PDF (official.nba.com, free; updates through the day before and day of game)
cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial)
nba.injuries_pit.why: Own status vintage sets participation (void or zero-minute branch) and teammate status vintages set who takes the drives and rim attempts that generate shooting fouls; previously unattached.

nba.teammate_absence_shift.label: With/without teammate splits: usage, minutes and stat redistribution
nba.teammate_absence_shift.mechanism: When key teammates are out, shot attempts, ball-handling, and rebound opportunities redistribute to the remaining players in a structured way (not evenly).
nba.teammate_absence_shift.rationale: This is the largest edge source for props: a lead guard out raises the backup guard's usage and assists, but a primary scorer out lowers assists for his passing partner (fewer converted passes). Direction depends on whether the absent player consumes the stat (usage, rebounds) or produces teammates' stat conversion (shooters). Subtle: with/without samples are small and confounded by opponent and by injuries to multiple players; use hierarchical shrinkage and role-based priors.
nba.teammate_absence_shift.measurement: Per player: stat per minute and minutes with teammate X on/off the roster, over games where X missed; hierarchical shrinkage to a role-based redistribution model (usage, ball handling, rebound share absorbed); evaluate for combinations of absences.
free_sources: PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)
nba.teammate_absence_shift.why: With/without splits of teammates' absence on a player's drives, rim attempts and free-throw trips; the usage-redistribution channel for free-throw attempts.

nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.label: Ratings-based blowout probability and starter-minutes-vs-margin curve (market-free)
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.mechanism: Rebuilds the blowout risk from team strength and rotation history instead of the closing spread: a ratings-implied expected margin and margin spread give P(large lead), and a coach/player minutes-versus-margin curve converts each margin path into expected minutes lost by starters and gained by bench players.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.rationale: The catalog input nba.garbage is defined from the closing spread, which is a market price and so a benchmark, not an input. The causal quantity is the chance that the margin passes the coach's pull threshold early enough to matter, and how much playing time each player then loses. Subtle: the loss depends on when the lead arrives (a 20-point lead entering Q4 removes far more starter minutes than one reached with 3 minutes left), on the coach, and on whether the trailing team also pulls starters, so the curve must be conditional on the margin path and not only on the final margin.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.measurement: Step 1, expected margin: mu = (NetRtg_home_adj - NetRtg_away_adj) * expected_possessions/100 + home_adv, where NetRtg_adj is the as-of-tipoff opponent-adjusted net rating from nba.off_rtg and nba.def_rtg (ridge regression on game point differential, half-life about 25 games, shrunk to the preseason prior with n_prior about 20 games as a placeholder to be fitted), adjusted for the confirmed unavailable players via nba.lineup_adj_rating, home_adv fitted on the last 5 seasons (about 2 points). Step 2, margin spread: sd_margin fitted on 5 seasons of residuals of final margin versus mu (league-wide roughly 12-13 points, to be estimated, with a heavier empirical tail than normal). Step 3: P(final |margin| >= 15/20/25) and P(|lead| >= 15/20 entering Q4) from the empirical residual distribution around mu. Step 4, minutes curve: from play-by-play stints, per team-season, expected minutes of each rotation player conditional on margin entering Q4 in bins (0-9, 10-14, 15-19, 20+), shrunk toward the league curve with k about 30 blowout games. Output per player: expected minutes lost and the probability of falling below a stated minutes level. No closing line or other price is used; the spread is retained only to benchmark calibration of step 3.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com leaguegamelog (team game logs, free, undocumented, rate-limited)

raw_data: team-game final margins and opponent-adjusted ratings as of tipoff (5 seasons)

nba.ft_attempts.reason: Attempt rate is the dominant factor, but the entry mixes FT% and foul rates in one input; split into trip structure and skill posterior.

nba.minutes.reason: Floor time scales exposure, but late-game minutes (which carry the most free throws) matter more than total minutes.

nba.referee_crew.reason: Crew foul tendency shifts attempts; the effect is concentrated in rim attackers and is known only on game day.

nba.fouls_ft.reason: Defined as foul drawing, free-throw rate and crew; foul drawing and rate duplicate ft_attempts and the crew part duplicates referee_crew.

nba.late_game_script.reason: The close-game fouling tail is real; as stated it lacks a target-selection mechanism, now provided by the intentional-foul target input.

nba.usage.reason: Usage mixes shot attempts and turnovers; for free throws the relevant measure is drives and post touches, which usage only proxies.

nba.shot_profile.reason: Rim attack share predicts shooting fouls; zone defence allowed informs opponent exposure.

nba.player_shooting_regression.reason: Shrinking FT% to career talent is correct, but it duplicates the skill posterior in function; FT% regresses little because it is a stable skill.

nba.garbage.reason: Catalog definition is 'Blowout / garbage-time probability from spread' (measurement: P(final |margin| > 15/20/25) as a function of the closing spread), so as defined it is market-derived and only a calibration benchmark; the blowout-minutes mechanism is carried by the market-free nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve (ratings-implied margin plus coach minutes-versus-margin curve).

nba.stat_dist.reason: The attempt-plus-binomial structure is the main distribution requirement; the entry names it but the trip clustering has to be added.

nba.stat_corrections.reason: Corrections rarely change free-throw counts, so the effect is only settlement-label noise.

nba.pace.reason: Pace scales attempts only slightly for a given role because free throws are driven by contact events, not possessions in the abstract.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price path for the free-throws-made ladder; useful to see when information was absorbed and for calibration labels, but it is an observation of the market, never an explanatory driver of the outcome.

m.rules_text.reason: Versioned rules text defines the settled quantity for the free-throws-made ladder; wording changes between series are the only way to know the target variable, so it is a required contract input, not a feature.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook price for the free-throws-made ladder is a market-derived quantity; keep as a comparison benchmark to measure disagreement, do not use as an input to the probability model.

nba.market_calibration_bias.reason: Price-bucket miscalibration for the free-throws-made ladder is measured on Kalshi prices, so it is a market-derived correction layer applied after a probability exists, not an input.

m.volume_oi.reason: Volume/open interest for the free-throws-made ladder measures liquidity and attention; market-derived and not a driver of the outcome, usable only to discount thin quotes.

m.trade_tape.reason: Trade prints for the free-throws-made ladder are market microstructure; informed-flow inference from them is speculative and cannot be a causal input.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Settled value and timestamp for the free-throws-made ladder are labels for calibration and need reconciling against the named source; not a pregame input.

interactions.mechanism: Crew whistle scales shooting-foul rates, and attempts scale with the player's rim and post volume, so the crew effect is multiplicative with exposure: a rim attacker gains more from a high-foul crew than a spot-up shooter.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact crew foul index with drives per minute and test the slope in a Poisson regression of trips.

interactions.mechanism: Hack-a policies are triggered when a player's free-throw percentage is below about 60% and the game is within a possession or two; outside that state the target probability is near zero.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the target probability by FT% bucket and margin to find the thresholds.

interactions.mechanism: The variance of makes depends on both attempts and rate: for a 60% shooter the binomial variance per attempt is larger than for an 85% shooter, so high-volume poor shooters have a wider count distribution than high-volume good shooters with the same mean.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare residual variance of makes across FT% terciles at the same expected attempts.

interactions.mechanism: The bonus effect applies in the minutes after the opponent reaches five team fouls in the period, so attempts depend on when in the quarter the player is on court; a player resting in late quarters misses the bonus window.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare FTA per minute in bonus versus non-bonus minutes by player and quarter.

interactions.mechanism: In a close game the last minutes produce many free throws for ball handlers, while in a blowout those minutes are played by bench players and no intentional fouls occur; the regime depends on the margin at 5:00 left.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare attempts in the last five minutes conditional on margin buckets.

nonlinearities.shape: Binomial variance p(1-p), maximal near 0.5
nonlinearities.why: The uncertainty of makes given attempts is largest for poor shooters, so the response of P(N+) to attempts differs by percentage.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold in FT% near 0.60 and in margin within about 6
nonlinearities.why: Target probability is near zero above the threshold and then jumps, so linear FT% effects misprice both ends.

nonlinearities.shape: Compound (clustered) count with 1-3 attempts per trip
nonlinearities.why: Attempts arrive in pairs and triples, giving a variance higher than Poisson and a lattice that matters at specific N.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in late-game minutes
nonlinearities.why: The last five minutes are about 10% of the 48 game minutes (roughly 12-15% of a star's minutes in a close game) yet carry a disproportionate share of his free throws, perhaps 20-25% (recalled, unsourced), so total minutes understate the weight of the closing period.

contract.settlement_definition: After the reconciliation this key holds six live series: player head-to-heads KXNBAH2HPRA (rules sampled), KXNBAH2HPTS and KXNBAH2H3PT (TITLE_ONLY), and series markets KXNBASERIESPTSLEADER, KXNBASERIESREBLEADER and KXNBAPTSALLGAMES (TITLE_ONLY). The sampled head-to-head settles Yes if player A records more combined points, rebounds and assists than player B in the full game (overtime included), resolves 50/50 on an exact tie, and resolves to a fair price if either player does not enter or the game is cancelled or postponed more than two weeks. The series leader and points-in-every-game definitions (tie rule, games missed, which games of the series count) are unseen and CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS; whether the TITLE_ONLY head-to-heads copy the PRA wording is assumed, not verified.

rules_evidence.quote: records more combined points, rebounds, and assists than Donovan Mitchell in the full game
rules_evidence.establishes: The head-to-head compares two players' single-game PRA totals over the full game, so overtime counts and the target is the sign of a difference of two correlated counts.

rules_evidence.quote: If both players enter the game and record an equal number of combined points, rebounds, and assists, then all markets resolve to 50/50.
rules_evidence.establishes: A tie settles at 50/50, so the tie mass is worth half a contract to each side rather than No or a void.

rules_evidence.quote: If one or both players do not enter the Cleveland vs New York professional basketball game originally scheduled for May 22, 2026, or the game is cancelled or postponed more than two weeks
rules_evidence.establishes: If either player does not enter, or the game slips more than two weeks, the market resolves to a fair price, so both players' availability is a void state, not a loss, and the postponement window is two weeks, not 48 hours.

variants_and_edge_cases: Tie in a head-to-head: the sampled KXNBAH2HPRA resolves an exact tie 50/50; for low-count stats like threes the tie mass is large (12-20%), so if the TITLE_ONLY KXNBAH2H3PT uses the same 50/50 rule each side holds half the tie mass, while a No or void rule would move the price materially.

One player does not play: the sampled head-to-head resolves to a fair price if either player does not enter, so availability of both players is a void state; the postponement window is two weeks, unlike the 48 hours of single-game ladders.
Series total versus average: a total depends on games played and a denominator for an average depends on games played, so a player who misses games alters the two differently.
Series length is random (4 to 7 games); whether the market is defined on all games of a series or on a fixed number of games is unseen.
Summer League games have different minute rules, game length and rosters; stats may be on a different official source with different correction timing.

Default tie scenarios to price until the rule is read: tie resolves No, tie voids at fair price, or tie splits 50/50. Independent-Poisson (Skellam) tie mass for made threes is about 21% at a mean of 2 each, 17% at 3, 14% at 4 and 13% at 5; overdispersion lowers it and positive pace correlation raises it, so 12-20% is the working range.

Series leader markets (KXNBASERIESPTSLEADER, KXNBASERIESREBLEADER) take the maximum over every rotation player of both teams, not a pairwise comparison, and KXNBAPTSALLGAMES needs a threshold met in every game of a random-length series; both are covered by stage s6 and their wording is unseen.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official box scores per game (NBA.com) for regular-season and playoff games; the sampled head-to-head uses the full game including overtime.

mechanism.summary: The three variants share one structure: a comparison or accumulation of player-game counts where the quantity of interest is the distribution of a difference or a sum rather than a threshold on one count. For a head-to-head the difference X_A - X_B has a mean given by the two players' expected counts and a variance that depends on each count's variance and on their correlation, which differs by pair type: same-team players are negatively associated at fixed team output because they split the same shots, rebounds and assists, opposing players are positively associated through shared pace, and players in different games are independent. A tie is possible for integer counts and its probability depends on the discreteness. For a series, the sum runs over a random number of games (the series length is itself uncertain and depends on the team strengths), each game's minutes are inflated in the playoffs, injuries attrite exposure, and the games are not independent because opposing coaches adjust. Summer League adds unstable rosters, announced minute plans, and rookies who play a fraction of the games. So the key information is exposure (games and minutes), dependence between the two sides, and discreteness at ties. Two further live series types are not pairwise: a series stat leader is the maximum of many players' cumulative totals over a random number of shared games, and points in every game is a run of threshold hits that any cold night or missed game breaks (stage s6).

stages.name: Exposure: games played and presence of both players
stages.description: Both players must play for a comparison to be meaningful, and in a series the number of games played by each depends on series length, injuries and rest decisions. A star out for part of a series reduces his total; the head-to-head may void or favour the player who plays. Exposure is the product of the number of games in the series (random) and the probability of availability in each game (autocorrelated through injuries).
stages.distribution: Series length P(4,5,6,7) with mean about 5.7 for evenly matched teams and 4.8 for mismatches; availability per game with persistence across games.

stages.name: Minutes and role in each game
stages.description: For each player the minutes mixture defines how many opportunities he has; in the playoffs the rotation tightens and stars play 38-42 minutes, so per-game counts inflate relative to the regular season, while in Summer League minutes are set by a plan, rookies may be capped and veterans may be rested in back-to-back games. Minutes are correlated across the two players when they are teammates in the same blowout or in opposing teams in the same game flow.
stages.distribution: Truncated normal in the playoffs (sd 3-4 minutes) versus bimodal in Summer League (limited or full minutes); correlation of minutes between the two players depends on the pair type.

stages.name: Per-minute rates and the opponent assignment
stages.description: Per-minute stat rates come from the player's usage and role, adjusted for the opponent's defence by position and, in series, by the primary defender assigned to him; the playoff matchup assignments suppress or boost a star's counts in a way not visible in regular-season splits. Across games in a series coaches adjust coverage so the effect changes over the series.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed counts around a rate that is itself shifted by matchup assignments; matchup shifts of 5-15% of the stat in a series (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED).

stages.name: Dependence between the two counts and ties
stages.description: The difference distribution depends on the correlation of the two players' counts: for opposing players it is positive through pace and through shared game script, shrinking the difference variance; for teammates it is negative at fixed team output (one player's shot is not the other's) but positive through team pace, so the net sign depends on the stat. With integer counts, ties have positive probability, 12-20% for made threes and a bit lower for assists, and the tie rule matters.
stages.distribution: Difference of two overdispersed counts with correlation from about -0.2 (teammates, shot-based stats) to +0.3 (opponents, pace-driven stats); discrete with a mass at zero.

stages.name: Summer League and series settlement structure
stages.description: Summer League results hinge on roster churn, unannounced minute plans and game participation (top picks play two or three games, others play five), with different stats sources and game lengths. For series totals and averages the settled quantity aggregates over a random exposure, so the pmf is a compound distribution and averages involve a random denominator. Each variant has its own settlement logic and none of the current inputs is attached to the Summer League game-selection pattern.
stages.distribution: Compound distribution (random games times random per-game counts); Summer League participation is a discrete choice with strong draft-slot dependence.

stages.name: Series leader maximum and every-game threshold runs
stages.description: A series points or rebounds leader is the argmax of cumulative totals across both rosters over four to seven games, so it is decided among the top two or three producers per team by their expected per-game rate times games played, with injuries that remove a candidate for games reshuffling the field and a tie possible at the top. Points in every game is the probability that a per-game threshold is met in each game of a series whose length is itself random, so a longer series lowers it geometrically, a single missed game or foul-trouble night breaks it, and the per-game hits are positively correlated through role and health.
stages.distribution: Leader: categorical over about six serious candidates, sharper than a single-game leader because summing 4-7 games cuts noise. Every-game: product of correlated per-game Bernoullis over a 4-7 game random length, so mass falls roughly geometrically in series length.

talent_strength.note: Player rates in the named stat.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent defence by position and playoff assignments.

availability_news.note: Both players' status and exposure over a series.

environment.note: Venue and altitude affect both players in the same game in the same way for opposing pairs and are second-order for a comparison of two counts; no separate environmental input is justified.

efficiency_conversion.note: Shooting-luck regression of recent 3P% or FG% toward talent and shot quality sets the per-attempt rate for threes and points comparisons; its extension to series-long shrinkage is untested (u4).

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, game selection and series elimination states.

officiating_rules.note: Referee crew effects on foul-based stats exist but are shared by both players in a game for opposing pairs, and no separate officiating input is justified for a difference between two counts.

settlement_contract.note: No live series or rule text exists for player head-to-head, series or Summer League markets; tie, void, denominator and overtime rules are unknown.

nba.pair_difference_correlation.label: Pair-type correlation of player stat residuals
nba.pair_difference_correlation.mechanism: The correlation between two players' counts differs by pair type (teammates, opponents, separate games) and by stat.
nba.pair_difference_correlation.rationale: The draft says positive correlation through game script, but for teammates the allocation effect is negative; a single sign misprices the difference variance and tie mass.
nba.pair_difference_correlation.measurement: For stat s and pair type, compute the correlation of residuals (after removing player and opponent effects and minutes) over 5 seasons for pairs of similar roles; pool in role-pair cells with shrinkage k=60 games; report the correlation and the implied variance of the difference var = var_A + var_B - 2 rho sd_A sd_B; produce P(A > B), P(tie), P(B > A) via a bivariate negative-binomial.
raw_data: player-game stats with team and opponent
nba.pair_difference_correlation.why: Head-to-head price depends mostly on the difference variance and tie mass, which the correlation sets.

nba.series_player_exposure.label: Expected games and minutes exposure over a series
nba.series_player_exposure.mechanism: Series totals depend on the number of games, availability in each, and playoff minutes inflation.
nba.series_player_exposure.rationale: The draft has a series model for the number of games but no link to each player's exposure, including injuries across games and early eliminations.
nba.series_player_exposure.measurement: E[games] = Σ_k P(series length = k) × k; exposure_i = Σ_games P(player i plays game g | series length) × expected minutes_g (playoff inflation factor from role-specific ratio of playoff to regular-season minutes over 10 seasons, shrunk with k=8 players); include injury persistence (probability of playing game g+1 given absent in g about 0.6, estimated); output exposure distribution (mean, sd).
nba.series_player_exposure.why: A total or an average depends on games played, and an average has a random denominator.

nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.label: Playoff matchup assignment shift (primary defender effect)
nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.mechanism: In a series the primary defenders assigned to stars shift counts relative to regular-season rates, adjusted game by game.
nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.rationale: Regular-season position-based opponent allowances miss the specific defender and the series adaptation. The 5-15% shift magnitude is SOURCE_UNVERIFIED (recalled, not estimated).
nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.measurement: From tracking matchup data compute for each offensive player the points/assists per 100 possessions guarded by each defender (min 50 possessions) with shrinkage to the defender's overall effect (k=100 possessions); for a series use the expected share of possessions by defender from the last regular-season meeting and playoffs-to-date; shift = Σ share × (matchup rate - baseline); update after each series game with half-life 2 games.
nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.why: Stars' series counts depend on who guards them, but the free source (nba_api leagueseasonmatchups) is a season-type aggregate and game-level playoff assignments are not shown to be available, so the input is context only until the source is verified.

nba.summer_league_game_selection_pattern.label: Summer League game selection and minutes cap pattern
nba.summer_league_game_selection_pattern.mechanism: Participation and minutes in Summer League depend on draft slot, contract status and team plans, with top picks playing fewer games and veterans resting.
nba.summer_league_game_selection_pattern.rationale: Summer League exposure is the main variance of its stat markets, and none of the current inputs gives the probability that a player plays a given game.
nba.summer_league_game_selection_pattern.measurement: Per player: P(plays game g) by draft slot bucket (top 5, 6-14, 15-30, second round, undrafted, veteran) from the last 6 Summer Leagues; minutes distribution per game conditional on playing; adjust for team announcements (coded 0/0.5/1) and for back-to-back games; combine to a distribution of games played and total minutes.
raw_data: Summer League game logs with draft slot
nba.summer_league_game_selection_pattern.why: Summer League props and head-to-heads are decided by participation first.

nba.player_shooting_regression.label: Player shooting luck vs expectation (3P%, FG%, FT%)
nba.player_shooting_regression.mechanism: Hot or cold stretches in 3P%/FG%/FT% mostly regress to a player's shot-quality-adjusted talent, so recent form overstates the next game's expected efficiency.
nba.player_shooting_regression.rationale: Markets and naive models overweight recent hot shooting; true talent is better estimated by priors from career, volume and shot openness. FT% stabilizes faster than 3P%. Subtle: real changes (mechanics, injury recovery, role) exist, so shrinkage weight should depend on sample size and change signals.
nba.player_shooting_regression.measurement: Beta-binomial shrinkage with prior mean = career/role expectation and prior strength set empirically per stat (3P ~ 300-500 att, FT ~ 100-150 att); compare recent vs shrunk estimate; include shot-quality (openness) adjustment.
free_sources: PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)
nba.player_shooting_regression.why: The compared stat is often made threes (the only live head-to-head series is KXNBAH2H3PT), where three-point shooting luck dominates the variance of the difference and the tie mass; the regression of recent 3P% to talent gives the per-attempt rate.

nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.label: Ratings-based blowout probability and starter-minutes-vs-margin curve (market-free)
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.mechanism: Rebuilds the blowout risk from team strength and rotation history instead of the closing spread: a ratings-implied expected margin and margin spread give P(large lead), and a coach/player minutes-versus-margin curve converts each margin path into expected minutes lost by starters and gained by bench players.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.rationale: The catalog input nba.garbage is defined from the closing spread, which is a market price and so a benchmark, not an input. The causal quantity is the chance that the margin passes the coach's pull threshold early enough to matter, and how much playing time each player then loses. Subtle: the loss depends on when the lead arrives (a 20-point lead entering Q4 removes far more starter minutes than one reached with 3 minutes left), on the coach, and on whether the trailing team also pulls starters, so the curve must be conditional on the margin path and not only on the final margin.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.measurement: Step 1, expected margin: mu = (NetRtg_home_adj - NetRtg_away_adj) * expected_possessions/100 + home_adv, where NetRtg_adj is the as-of-tipoff opponent-adjusted net rating from nba.off_rtg and nba.def_rtg (ridge regression on game point differential, half-life about 25 games, shrunk to the preseason prior with n_prior about 20 games as a placeholder to be fitted), adjusted for the confirmed unavailable players via nba.lineup_adj_rating, home_adv fitted on the last 5 seasons (about 2 points). Step 2, margin spread: sd_margin fitted on 5 seasons of residuals of final margin versus mu (league-wide roughly 12-13 points, to be estimated, with a heavier empirical tail than normal). Step 3: P(final |margin| >= 15/20/25) and P(|lead| >= 15/20 entering Q4) from the empirical residual distribution around mu. Step 4, minutes curve: from play-by-play stints, per team-season, expected minutes of each rotation player conditional on margin entering Q4 in bins (0-9, 10-14, 15-19, 20+), shrunk toward the league curve with k about 30 blowout games. Output per player: expected minutes lost and the probability of falling below a stated minutes level. No closing line or other price is used; the spread is retained only to benchmark calibration of step 3.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com leaguegamelog (team game logs, free, undocumented, rate-limited)
cdn.nba.com liveData playbyplay JSON (substitutions with score, free, unofficial)
Basketball-Reference game logs and play-by-play (free, polite scraping)
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.why: Replaces the spread-based nba.garbage in player_h2h_series_stats: blowout truncation of the relevant players' minutes from own ratings and the coach's pull curve, with no closing line used.
raw_data: team-game final margins and opponent-adjusted ratings as of tipoff (5 seasons)
play-by-play substitution stints with margin entering Q4 (per team-season)

nba.series_stat_leader_model.label: Playoff-series stat-leader probability (max of cumulative totals across both rosters, with ties)
nba.series_stat_leader_model.mechanism: The series leader is the player with the largest cumulative points or rebounds over the series, the maximum of about 16-20 rotation players' totals over a random number of shared games, correlated through series length and pace and negatively within a team.
nba.series_stat_leader_model.rationale: KXNBASERIESPTSLEADER and KXNBASERIESREBLEADER are live under this key and are not pairwise head-to-heads. Leadership concentrates on each team's top producers, and the relevant quantity is the gap in expected per-game rate times games played; summing 4-7 games reduces noise so favourites are stronger than in a single-game leader market, while an injury that costs a candidate one or two games shifts mass sharply. The tie rule is unseen.
nba.series_stat_leader_model.measurement: Simulate each series game by game: series length and winner from nba.series_model; per-player per-game counts from negative-binomial draws on a playoff-minutes scenario (rotation tightening, per-game injury hazard), with per-player rates shrunk to a role prior with k=10 games; compute P(player holds the maximum cumulative total) and P(tie at the maximum) from at least 20,000 simulated series. Calibrate on 15 seasons of playoff series (leader identity against pre-series expected rank, Brier score). As-of: before game 1, then updated after each game with realised totals.
raw_data: playoff player-game box scores (points, rebounds, minutes) for 15 seasons
nba.series_stat_leader_model.why: Series leader markets need the probability of being the maximum among many players' series totals, which pairwise difference inputs do not give.

nba.streak_hit_persistence.label: Game-to-game persistence of threshold hits and streak-break hazard (DNP, rest, matchup)
nba.streak_hit_persistence.mechanism: A streak of N games meeting a threshold is a run-length process whose per-game hit probability varies with minutes and rest and which is broken by any DNP or rest night.
nba.streak_hit_persistence.rationale: Treating hits as independent with the season-average rate understates both streak and break risk; minutes and rest dependencies create positive autocorrelation within a stretch, and the specific rule (whether inactive games break the streak) changes everything.
nba.streak_hit_persistence.measurement: For each player estimate a logistic model of threshold hit on minutes projection, rest days, opponent defensive rating and lag-1 hit (to capture persistence beyond minutes) over a 3-season window; compute probability of a run of length at least N via a Markov chain with state = current run length and per-game hit probability from the model; add break hazard per game from injury/rest model. Adjust for the rule on inactive games (counts as break, skip, or void).
nba.streak_hit_persistence.why: KXNBAPTSALLGAMES is a run of per-game threshold hits over a series that a missed game or cold night breaks, which is exactly the run-length process this input models.
raw_data: player-game points and minutes with rest and DNP flags (3 seasons)

nba.minutes.reason: Minutes in each game feed both players' counts; the distribution differs by setting (playoff vs Summer League) and needs the correlation between the two players' minutes.

nba.usage.reason: Usage is a shot-based opportunity measure; for assists or rebounds comparisons it is the wrong driver, so stat-specific opportunity measures are needed.

nba.stat_dist.reason: Per-stat count marginals are needed for the difference and sum distributions; they do not give dependence between the two players.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Both players' status is the first gate and, for a series, status over several games with persistence matters.

nba.series_model.reason: Series length distribution is necessary for totals and averages; labelled secondary but it sets exposure and so is primary for series variants.

nba.playoff_rotation.reason: Playoff minute inflation and rotation tightening is a real effect, applying only to the series variant.

nba.summer_league_minutes.reason: Minute plans are central for Summer League but are announced late; the game-selection pattern is a separate factor.

nba.opp_def_pos.reason: Position-based allowances are coarse and unstable, so they act only as the regular-season and Summer League prior; in a series the assigned-defender input is meant to override them, and the matchup interaction tests exactly whether the position prior still carries information.

nba.pace.reason: Shared pace correlates opposing players' counts, which narrows the difference variance; the effect size is modest.

nba.garbage.reason: Catalog definition is 'Blowout / garbage-time probability from spread' (measurement: P(final |margin| > 15/20/25) as a function of the closing spread), so as defined it is market-derived and only a calibration benchmark; the blowout-minutes mechanism is carried by the market-free nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve (ratings-implied margin plus coach minutes-versus-margin curve).

nba.late_game_script.reason: Intentional-foul effects matter for free-throw-related stats only; weak for most compared stats.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price path for the player head-to-head and series stat markets; useful to see when information was absorbed and for calibration labels, but it is an observation of the market, never an explanatory driver of the outcome.

m.rules_text.reason: Versioned rules text defines the settled quantity for the player head-to-head and series stat markets; wording changes between series are the only way to know the target variable, so it is a required contract input, not a feature.

interactions.mechanism: The variance of a difference is var_A + var_B minus twice the covariance, so a positive correlation between opposing players narrows the distribution and raises tie probability, while a negative correlation between teammates widens it; the pair type reverses the effect of the same marginals.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the correlation by pair type and test calibration of P(tie) and P(A>B) on held-out pairs.

interactions.mechanism: A series total is a sum over a random number of games, so a longer series disproportionately raises the upper tail; mean games enter linearly but sd of the total depends on the variance of game counts, which is larger for even matchups than for mismatches.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate series totals under different series length distributions and compare the upper-quantile differences.

interactions.mechanism: If a star is lost for the rest of a series his total stops accumulating and the head-to-head may void; the probability of staying healthy across games declines multiplicatively with persistence, creating a threshold-like drop in total after the first injury.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit a model of games played given injury status after game 1 and compare series totals with and without an injury.

interactions.mechanism: The position-based allowance matters only if the assigned defender follows the position; when a coach assigns a wing stopper to a guard the position average is wrong, so the assignment overrides it.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare predictions using position allowance versus assigned-defender allowance on past series.

interactions.mechanism: A top pick plays a fraction of Summer League games with capped minutes, while a veteran plays all games with full minutes, so stat accumulation is a regime-dependent mixture that depends on the draft-slot bucket.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare per-game minutes and games played across draft-slot buckets for the last six Summer Leagues.

nonlinearities.shape: Discrete, right-skewed series length (4 to 7)
nonlinearities.why: The number of games has a lattice distribution that is bimodal for mismatches and concentrated at 6-7 for even teams, so linearising by an expected length misprices totals.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating minutes inflation near 40
nonlinearities.why: Playoff minutes for stars rise from about 35 to about 40 and cannot rise further, so the inflation factor saturates with role intensity.

nonlinearities.shape: Lattice with a tie mass at zero difference
nonlinearities.why: For low counts (threes, assists) the difference has a notable mass exactly at zero (about 12-20% for threes), so a continuous approximation underprices ties.

nonlinearities.shape: Bimodal minutes (capped versus full)
nonlinearities.why: Summer League minutes cluster at a cap for rookies and at a high value for veterans, so mean minutes are rarely observed.
